import sys, json, uuid, hashlib, datetime, re, time, math

# >>> content-budget v1 (R-IG-1, GH #1085)
CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 3


def budget_chars(input_soft, share):
    """Characters a producer may hand a model whose usable window is
    `input_soft` tokens (the catalog row, cut by the curator), for a section
    that takes `share` of that window. None when no window is known: the
    producer then delivers its content whole."""
    try:
        soft = int(float(input_soft))
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None
    if soft <= 0:
        return None
    return int(soft * share * CHARS_PER_TOKEN)


def clip(text, limit, hint="budget of the window"):
    """`text` whole when it fits `limit` (None: no limit); else its head and
    a mark naming what was shown, the total and how to get the rest."""
    text = "" if text is None else str(text)
    if limit is None or len(text) <= limit:
        return text
    limit = max(0, int(limit))
    return text[:limit] + "...[cut: %d of %d chars shown; %s]" % (
        limit, len(text), hint)

# THE WINDOW OF ONE MODEL (curator, GH #888; a policy per role, GH #892). This
# cell decides what the model behind the hive sees on every call and keeps the
# record of what it saw:
#
#   * the hot path (`win-hashes` -> `win`): the system part is the `slots` the
#     ledger holds (plus the pins and the tool stubs of the current plan) and
#     the slots of the call's own session it was parked with, sent only when a
#     family changed and then as a `$replace` root -- the families that carry
#     rows of a round (`history`, `pinned`) and those that hold a session's
#     slots (`roster`, `consult`, `instructions`) on every call (GH #925);
#     the messages are
#     the wall after the plan's cover, in `seq` order, over every session
#     (OR-KX-K4), each shown the way the plan says. Deterministic, no model call.
#     Between two rebuilds only the END of the window moves (OR-KX-G4) -- a
#     provider's prefix cache keys on exactly that, so everything that changes a
#     block in the middle (a release, a shrunk tool result, a stub, a pin moving
#     into the system part, an expiry) is decided at a rebuild -- and at one
#     second place: the session boundary (GH #1335, `session_bounds`) frames
#     the person's texts of other sessions, so a block in the middle changes
#     at the first call of a new session and when another session first
#     stands in the wall.
#   * the record: one `calls` row and its `call_blocks` per call, written in
#     the same emission as the call itself, BEFORE the brain has it. A block the
#     window shows in another form than the wall holds it (its short id in
#     front, a one-line form) is a block of kind `view`, so the record names
#     only blocks the ledger holds and rebuilds the request byte for byte.
#   * the tap (`tap`): the usage the brain reported fills that row later, and
#     a stamped `cache_expires_at` orders the clock: ONE standing order per
#     round under an id of that round (`clock_id`), re-armed per call (`add`
#     with `rearm`, GH #904), carrying the call's round to the rebuild it
#     starts (GH #925).
#   * the rebuild (`rb-*`, `sum`): when the cache has gone cold or the prompt
#     crossed a line of the model's package (`input_soft`, GH #1038) -- without
#     one, `compress_at` of the model's own window --, the plan of the window
#     is made anew from the role's
#     knobs (`window_plan`): the segments in the horizon in their tier form,
#     the newest `keep_recent` rounds raw, the model's own releases and pins
#     applied, and -- when the plan is still over `rebuild_to` of the usable
#     window -- old tool results shrunk, unused tools stubbed and the summary
#     given up, in that order. A summary is made by `./summarizer` -- never in
#     the hot path, at most one rebuild per round at a time (OR-KX-K5), and a
#     failed summary leaves the window as it was (OR-KX-K6). A rebuild reads
#     only the rows of the round its call was made in (`rebuild_where`, GH
#     #932 review I-1): the cut, the rows held, the ages, the shrunk results
#     and the aim follow the rows that round may see, and a release or pin of
#     another round is kept in the plan per audience (`marks_on`) but never
#     shapes a window of a round that may not see it.
#   * ONE PLAN PER ROUND (GH #943): the plan, the rebuild lock, the call the
#     clock is armed for, the pending actions, the summary slot and its
#     binding are state keyed by `round_key` -- the first 12 hex digits of
#     the sha256 of the canonical round; a call without a round has the key
#     of `[]`. Why: with one plan per hive, the cut (`cover`) and what was
#     shrunk or stubbed were set by the round whose call started the rebuild,

# THE AUDIENCE GATE (GH #925). Every row of `wall`, `calls`, `marks`,
# `summaries` and `pins` carries the audience of the round that caused it
# (`audience_set`, a canonical JSON array), and a reader hands a row to a round
# iff the row has one and it names `*` or holds the round as a subset -- the
# affinity rule (templates/affinity/README.md, GH #154/#306). The round is
# `context.audience_set` of the message being served: this hive's edges set
# and delete only `cur_*`, so it rides the context through every ledger round
# trip exactly like `cur_origin`, and it is never guessed from a row. These
# functions are the same text in every cell of this hive that writes or reads
# rows; a lock holds them to one table. A ledger read asks the store first
# (`round_where`, GH #932), so a row the round may not see never comes back,
# and the gate in Python stays as the second line.


def audience_of(value):
    """An audience in its canonical form -- a JSON array of strings, sorted,
    no duplicates, no whitespace -- or None when there is none. The round
    arrives as TEXT (a JSON array in a string) and a column comes back as
    text; a list is taken as it is. Absent, empty text, a scalar or
    unparsable text is NOT DECLARED: the empty list is a declared round, None
    is no round at all (affinity `as_set`, GH #306)."""
    if isinstance(value, str):
        if not value.strip():
            return None
        try:
            value = json.loads(value)
        except ValueError:
            return None
    if not isinstance(value, list):
        return None
    return json.dumps(sorted({str(x) for x in value if str(x)}), separators=(",", ":"))


def allowed(round_value, origin):
    """The gate: a row whose audience is `origin` may reach the round
    `round_value` iff both are declared and the origin names `*` or holds the
    round as a subset. A row from before the rule has no origin and never
    leaves (OR-BD-5); a round nobody declared passes nothing."""
    r, o = audience_of(round_value), audience_of(origin)
    if r is None or o is None:
        return False
    o = set(json.loads(o))
    return "*" in o or set(json.loads(r)) <= o


def passes(row, round_value, session):
    """One reader's verdict on one row. With a declared round it is the gate;
    without one, only a row of the running session that declares no round
    either (or names `*`) passes -- the window and the handover keep a
    round-less conversation going and show nothing from elsewhere (OR-BD-4).
    A row of a declared round never reaches a call nobody declared a round
    for, though it stands in the same session (review M-7: the words of {e,b}
    reached a round-less call of that session, and a round-less recall took
    the addendum of an {e,a} gap). A row that names no session never passes
    a round-less read."""
    if audience_of(round_value) is None:
        if not session or str(row.get("session_id") or "") != session:
            return False
        own = audience_of(row.get("audience_set"))
        return own is not None and (own == "[]" or "*" in json.loads(own))
    return allowed(round_value, row.get("audience_set"))


ROUNDLESS = ["[]", "[\"*\"]"]


def round_where(round_value, session):
    """The store half of the audience gate (GH #932): the `where` terms a
    ledger read adds so that only rows this round may see come back -- page
    bounds, `scanned`, window and renewal sizes and turn counts then hang on
    visible rows alone, and a hidden row costs nothing a reader can count.
    With a declared, non-empty round it is `covers` (the affinity rule in the
    store). Without one -- or with a declared EMPTY round, which `covers`
    refuses -- only rows of the running session that declare no round either
    (`[]`, PP-BD-12) or name `*` come back; a row from before the rule (NULL)
    never does. None: nothing may be read at all (no round and no session).
    The Python gate below stays as the second line."""
    r = audience_of(round_value)
    if r is not None and r != "[]":
        return {"audience_set": {"covers": json.loads(r)}}
    if not session:
        return None
    return {"session_id": session, "audience_set": {"in": list(ROUNDLESS)}}


def audience_meet(values):
    """The audience of a row made of other rows (a summary, a handover
    block): the INTERSECTION of its sources, so it can never be wider than
    any of them (OR-BD-3). A source naming `*` is neutral; one source without
    an audience, or no source at all, makes the result None."""
    out, universal = None, False
    for v in values:
        c = audience_of(v)
        if c is None:
            return None
        s = set(json.loads(c))
        if "*" in s:
            universal = True
            continue
        out = s if out is None else out & s
    if out is None:
        return '["*"]' if universal else None
    return json.dumps(sorted(out), separators=(",", ":"))


def meet_of_rows(values):
    """`audience_meet` for a row written from other rows (GH #932, PP-BD-12).
    Since PP-BD-12 `[]` marks a round-less row, which round-less calls of its
    session read; an EMPTY meet is that mark only when every source that
    names no `*` is round-less itself. An empty meet of declared rounds
    ({a} and {b}, or {e,a} and a round-less row) names nobody: None, and the
    row reaches no round -- before PP-BD-12 such a `[]` reached none either."""
    out = audience_meet(values)
    if out == "[]":
        for v in values:
            c = audience_of(v)
            if c is not None and c != "[]" and "*" not in json.loads(c):
                return None
    return out


# The round this message serves (GH #925, OR-BD.A.1): `context.audience_set`,
# read anew at every step and never from a row. Lower case on purpose: the
# pure half is loaded with the upper-case constants and without a context

the_round = ctx.get("audience_set")


def with_audience(row, value):
    """An insert row with the audience of the round `value` in its canonical
    form; a call without a round writes `[]` (PP-BD-12) -- the row declares
    no round, so a round-less read of its own session finds it through the
    store filter (`round_where`), and NULL is left to rows from before the
    rule (OR-BD-5)."""
    aud = audience_of(value)
    return dict(row, audience_set=aud if aud is not None else "[]")


def with_meet(row, value):
    """An insert row with an audience made of other rows (`audience_meet`):
    None there means NOT DETERMINABLE, not "no round" -- the column stays
    NULL and the row reaches no round (OR-BD-5, GH #932 keeps this apart
    from the round-less `[]` of `with_audience`)."""
    aud = audience_of(value)
    if aud is not None:
        row = dict(row, audience_set=aud)
    return row


def _knob(key, default):
    v = P.get(key, default)
    return default if v is None else v


def _int(key, default):
    v = _knob(key, default)
    if isinstance(v, str) and not v.strip():
        return default
    return int(float(v))

SHIPPED = {"compress_at": 0.5, "rebuild_to": 0, "keep_recent": 12,

def unset(v):
    return v is None or (isinstance(v, str) and not v.strip())


def knob_of(params, key):
    """One knob of `params`: the value set on it, else its shipped value."""
    params = params if isinstance(params, dict) else {}
    v = params.get(key)
    if unset(v):
        return SHIPPED[key]
    return v


def number_of(params, key):
    try:
        return float(knob_of(params, key))
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return float(SHIPPED[key])


def share_of(v):
    """A share knob that may stay empty (GH #1464, `cold_to`): a finite
    number or numeric string of 0 or more; None when unset, unparsable,
    infinite or below 0 -- the knob is then off and the rule of before
    stands (an infinite share broke `cold_aim_of` on `round(inf)`)."""
    if unset(v) or isinstance(v, bool):
        return None
    try:
        f = float(v)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None
    return f if math.isfinite(f) and f >= 0 else None


def switch_on(v):
    """One switch (#1370): JSON true, "1", "true" or "on" is on, anything else
    off -- the rule of the presenter's `knob()`. A set writes its switches as
    JSON true (soul2me 0.45 `04-assistant.json`), and `str(True)` is "True":
    a read `== "1"` kept them off without a word."""
    return str(v).strip().lower() in ("1", "true", "on")


def flag_of(params, key):
    v = knob_of(params, key)
    if isinstance(v, bool):
        return v
    return str(v).strip().lower() not in ["", "0", "false", "off", "no"]


def tiers_of(params):

    this policy does not know makes the shipped value stand, and says so."""

    items = v if isinstance(v, list) else str(v).split(",")
    out = [str(x).strip() for x in items if str(x).strip()]
    if not out or any(x not in TIER_FORMS for x in out):
        sys.stderr.write("curator/policy: tiers %r not understood -- the shipped value stands\n"
                         % (v,))
        out = [x.strip() for x in SHIPPED["tiers"].split(",")]
    return out

        h = SHIPPED["horizon"]
    return h

# cached window is not free: at a cached price of 10 % of the input price a

# them) is the rate the plan of a rebuild estimates a form with: the row's,
# never a second number of this cell's own (Fable review #5).
# GH #1431: `cost_cache_write` is the price of writing a rebuilt window into
# the provider's cache, and `price_tiers` (read by `price_steps_of`) the whole
# price ladder, the base step first -- a provider that bills a prompt over a
# step dearer bills the held window and the rebuilt one each at its own step.
LIMIT_KEYS = ("input_soft", "input_hard", "cost_in", "cost_cached_in", "cost_cache_write",
              "chars_per_token")

# THE WINDOW IS MEASURED, NEVER SUMMED, AND THE HARD LINE IS THE LLM CELL'S
# (GH #1038, KF1 review M2/M3). After a `length` continuation the llm cell
# reports `tokens_prompt` as the SUM of every call of the answer -- twice the
# window and more -- so the policy measures a window at what it sent: its own
# projection of the call (every system leaf and every message), estimated the
# way the llm cell estimates a request before it refuses one over
# `input_hard` (`estimate_tokens`, the token-estimate block below, GH #1098:
# one estimate for every template -- high on purpose). The window of a turn is the smaller of the two: the estimate
# stays above the real count, the sum far above it. And because the cell
# refuses on that estimate, not on measured tokens, `hard` is also due when
# the estimate of the NEXT window -- this one plus the answer -- reaches
# HARD_HEADROOM of `input_hard`: the tenth left over is for what the
# projection does not see (the provider request's own framing, the next turn,
# a tool result of the next iteration).
HARD_HEADROOM = 0.9

# >>> token-estimate v1 (GH #1098)
# The one token estimate of the templates: a request as the llm cell
# estimates it before it refuses one over `input_hard` (`window.rs`
# `estimate_prompt_tokens`) for a model whose catalogue row states no rates
# of its own -- UTF-8 bytes of every string and object key, 4 for a number
# or a bool, over CHARS_PER_TOKEN of the content-budget block (the same
# three bytes a token every budget of the templates is sized with), rounded
# up; a string starting `data:` (an inline image) counts IMAGE_TOKENS, the
# cell's own `llm::window::IMAGE_TOKENS`.
IMAGE_TOKENS = 1024


def estimate_tokens(value):
    """Tokens of `value` (any JSON value) by the rule above."""
    nbytes, images, todo = 0, 0, [value]
    while todo:
        v = todo.pop()
        if isinstance(v, str):
            if v.startswith("data:"):
                images += 1
            else:
                nbytes += len(v.encode("utf-8"))
        elif isinstance(v, dict):
            for k, x in v.items():
                nbytes += len(str(k).encode("utf-8"))
                todo.append(x)
        elif isinstance(v, (list, tuple)):
            todo.extend(v)
        elif isinstance(v, (bool, int, float)):
            nbytes += 4
    return tokens_of_bytes(nbytes) + images * IMAGE_TOKENS


def tokens_of_bytes(nbytes):
    """Tokens of `nbytes` bytes (or characters) of text: over
    CHARS_PER_TOKEN, rounded up."""
    return -(-max(0, int(nbytes)) // CHARS_PER_TOKEN)
# <<< token-estimate v1


def window_of(tokens_prompt, projected):
    """The window of a turn: the measured prompt, unless the policy's own
    projection of the call is smaller -- then the measure is a sum over a
    continuation, and the projection stands. Either alone when the other is
    missing; None with neither."""
    tp = tokens_prompt if isinstance(tokens_prompt, (int, float)) \
        and not isinstance(tokens_prompt, bool) and tokens_prompt > 0 else None
    est = projected if isinstance(projected, (int, float)) and projected > 0 else None
    if tp is None or est is None:
        return tp if est is None else est
    return min(tp, est)


def _price(v):
    """A price of a step as a float, None when it is no number or below 0."""
    if isinstance(v, bool) or not isinstance(v, (int, float)) or v != v or v < 0:
        return None
    return float(v)


def price_steps_of(v):
    """The price ladder off the tap (GH #1431, `hop.price_tiers`): the steps
    with a whole `above_input` of at least 0 and a `cost_in` above 0, each
    with its `cost_cached_in` / `cost_cache_write` when it names one (a
    cached price of 0 is a price), ordered by `above_input`. A step that is
    none of that is left out; no valid step is no ladder ([])."""
    out = []
    for s in v if isinstance(v, list) else []:
        if not isinstance(s, dict):
            continue
        above, ci = s.get("above_input"), _price(s.get("cost_in"))
        if isinstance(above, bool) or not isinstance(above, int) or above < 0 \
                or ci is None or ci <= 0:
            continue
        step = {"above_input": above, "cost_in": ci}
        for k in ("cost_cached_in", "cost_cache_write"):
            c = _price(s.get(k))
            if c is not None and (c > 0 or k == "cost_cached_in"):
                step[k] = c
        out.append(step)
    return sorted(out, key=lambda s: s["above_input"])


def limits_of(usage):
    """The answering model's limits and prices off the tap's usage: a value
    that is no number is absent, and so is one at or below zero -- except a
    cached price of 0, which is a price. The price ladder (GH #1431) only
    when the tap carries one."""
    out = {}
    for k in LIMIT_KEYS:
        v = (usage or {}).get(k)
        if v in (None, "") or isinstance(v, bool):
            continue
        try:
            n = float(v)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            continue
        if n > 0 or (n == 0 and k == "cost_cached_in"):
            out[k] = n
    steps = price_steps_of((usage or {}).get("price_tiers"))
    if steps:
        out["price_tiers"] = steps
    return out

# no llm-registry push reached -- every LLM cell of a satz provisioned without

# beside `input_soft_fallback`, each the row's own -- a template test holds

# a package -- reported by the model or set on the instance (`context_window`)
# -- is an old package, and the rule of before holds for it.
# `cost_cache_write` has no fallback param (OR-d38-1.k5.3): the fallback row
# carries no price ladder, and without one the cost rule never reads it.
FALLBACK_LIMITS = limits_of(dict((k, P.get(k + "_fallback")) for k in LIMIT_KEYS
                                 if k != "cost_cache_write"))
try:
    FALLBACK_TTL_S = max(0, int(float(P.get("cache_ttl_s_fallback") or 0)))
except (TypeError, ValueError):
    FALLBACK_TTL_S = 0
# The keys an answer of a model with a package carries (GH #1037).
PACKAGE_KEYS = ("input_soft", "context_window", "cache_expires_at")


# D58 target (GH #1483, contract points 1, 2, 5, 6, 7): what the curator
# holds of a target -- the name its composite wires a model cell under, which
# a curate names (`hop.target`) or the lead's verdict names (`target`) --
# lives in one family of state keys, read in one range read before the
# verdict (`w-cat`): `catalog:<target>` the row the cell reported, with its
# window profile and the order of its system part beside the row's fields
# (OR-d58-2.target.3), and `catalog:<target>:<field>` what the answers of the
# target said (`input_soft`, `input_hard`, `context_window`) and the session
# it was last asked in (`asked`). The curator keeps no list of targets and no
# built-in one: the family is what the cells told it. A call without a target
# keeps its answers' values under the empty name (`catalog::<field>`); the
# question to every cell at once is `catalog::asked` (OR-d58-2.target.21).
TARGET_FIELDS = ("input_soft", "input_hard", "context_window", "asked", "form")
# The most keys the range read takes (OR-d58-2.target.21): the store knows no
# upper bound beside a lower one, so the read runs from the family's first
# key in key order and stops here; five keys and a row per target (`form`,
# GH #1497: the rows its window was cut by on the plan that stands). The
# `form` key is a sixth key per target, so the read takes 10 targets whole,
# not 12 (a talky has 4); and as each `form` row holds the rows of every
# target, the bytes the read takes grow with the square of the targets.
TARGET_READ = 64


def target_key(target, field):
    """The state key of `field` of `target` (`catalog:<target>:<field>`)."""
    return CATALOG_KEY + target + ":" + field


def catalog_row(target, st):
    """The row the cell `target` reported, its profile and order beside it
    (`catalog:<target>`), {} when the state holds none."""
    row = loads(st.get(CATALOG_KEY + target, "") or "", {}) if target else {}
    return row if isinstance(row, dict) and str(row.get("model") or "") else {}


def held_targets(st):
    """The targets whose row `st` holds, in key order."""
    return sorted(k[len(CATALOG_KEY):] for k in st
                  if k.startswith(CATALOG_KEY) and ":" not in k[len(CATALOG_KEY):]
                  and catalog_row(k[len(CATALOG_KEY):], st))


# GH #1497: the order of a change of plan for a catalogue row that moved
# since a target's window was first cut on the plan that stands (`form_view`)
# -- a `curate_mark` of its own, so `./stats` counts it as a rebuild -- and
# the field of the projection (`est_row`) that carries the news to the tap.
# The rebuild it orders asks no summarizer and no model (phase `rb-data`,
# `collect_only`), but it is more than a new cut: the collection of the plan
# runs as well, warm cache or not (shrunk and released blocks, blocks past
# their time; `gc_on_cold` is not asked), so the window it makes may be
# shorter than the one before -- one cache write per target whose window
# the collection changes.
CATALOG_MARK = "catalog"
MOVED_FIELD = "catalog_moved"


# GH #1517 (d): the `owner` this hive's own cells book on
# the slot rows they write (`./push`, `./policy`) -- the one column that tells
# a slot the curator writes itself from a slot of another owner.
OWN_SLOT_OWNER = "curator"


def held_slot(r):
    """GH #1517 (d): whether the slot row `r` is one the curator holds back
    to the next change of plan -- a slot it writes itself (`owner` is
    `OWN_SLOT_OWNER`). A slot of any other owner (a pack, a collector) is a
    contract over content and stands in the next call as it always did
    (trust before the cache)."""
    path = str(r.get("path") or "")
    # One rule per kind of block, no list of names: the leaves of the family
    # `history` are lines of the rounds, not a slot of the plan -- they carry
    # the curator's `owner` too, but `turn_cut_slots` cuts them per turn by
    # their own rule, unchanged by this one; every other slot of the
    # curator's own is held.
    return bool(path) and not in_family(path, "history") \
        and str(r.get("owner") or "") == OWN_SLOT_OWNER


def form_slots(slot_rows):
    """GH #1517 (d): `{path: hash}` of the slots of the system part the cut
    holds to its state of the plan (`held_slot`), out of the rows a cut
    builds its system part from (`own_slots` of the round)."""
    out = {}
    for r in slot_rows:
        if held_slot(r):
            out[str(r.get("path") or "")] = str(r.get("hash") or "")
    return out


def form_bodies(slots, blocks):
    """GH #1517 (d): `{hash: body}` of the held slots `slots` (`form_slots`)
    out of the blocks a cut read (`blocks`, by hash): what the first cut on a
    state of the plan keeps, so that a slot that changes later still has the
    block it was cut with (`form_view`)."""
    out = {}
    for h in sorted(set((slots or {}).values())):
        body = str((blocks.get(h) or {}).get("body") or "")
        if body:
            out[h] = body
    return out


def form_view(target, st, epoch, slots=None, bodies=None):
    """`(view, record, moved, held, held_bodies)` of a call to `target` cut on the state of the plan
    `epoch` (GH #1497): the state `st` with the catalogue rows the cut reads
    -- the target's own, and every other target's for the slots they name
    and the wall's values -- as they stood when the target's window was
    first cut on this state of the plan (`catalog:<target>:form`). A row
    that arrived or changed since takes effect with the next change of plan,
    the one place a prefix may change. Measured in L1 (OR-58-182): the first
    call of a colony went out before any row (the question goes beside it,
    contract point 5), the rows came home before the second, and the second
    call, cut by them, began with another window -- the identity moved
    (`identity_budget`), the words got their short id (`short_ids`), the
    slot of another target left the system part: a prefix break without a
    rebuild in every structural run, the window 246 tokens shorter (19021
    -> 18775). `record` is the value to keep for the target when it is not
    the one kept (the first call on this state of the plan), else None;
    `moved` says that the rows as they stand differ from the kept ones --
    the call orders the change of plan that takes them on (`CATALOG_MARK`,
    the tap of its answer). The rows of EVERY target are compared, not only
    the ones the call reads: a row of another target that moved orders the
    change of plan as well. Only the first call of a turn orders it with
    `recall_in_wall` "1" (the turn's row, `turn_cut`); with "0" there is no
    such row, every call of a round can order it, and the change of plan can
    take effect inside a round that runs.

    GH #1517 (d): the slots of the system part the curator writes itself
    (`form_slots`, given as `slots`) are kept the same way. Measured in a
    run without a model: the slot `instructions.hygiene` that `./push`
    writes in the bundle of the first turn came home between the first and
    the second call of a freshly reset session, the second call carried it
    in its system part and broke the prefix without a rebuild (call 2
    `prefix_break` 1, in two sessions). `held` is the `{path: hash}` the target's window
    was first cut with on this state of the plan (None when the record holds
    none, or no `slots` were given); a slot that arrived or changed since
    takes effect with the next change of plan and orders it (`moved`).
    `held_bodies` is the `{hash: body}` of those slots as the first cut read
    them (`form_bodies`, given as `bodies`; kept in the record beside
    `slots`): a changed slot's row names its new block only (one row per
    path), so the block it was cut with comes from here until the change of
    plan. {} when the record keeps none."""
    rows_now = dict((CATALOG_KEY + t, st[CATALOG_KEY + t]) for t in held_targets(st))
    kept = loads(st.get(target_key(target, "form"), "") or "", {})
    if isinstance(kept, dict) and kept.get("epoch") == epoch \
            and isinstance(kept.get("rows"), dict):
        rows_kept = dict((k, str(v)) for k, v in kept["rows"].items()
                         if isinstance(k, str) and k.startswith(CATALOG_KEY))
        view = dict((k, v) for k, v in st.items() if k not in rows_now)
        view.update(rows_kept)
        held = kept.get("slots") if isinstance(kept.get("slots"), dict) else None
        if held is None or slots is None:
            return view, None, rows_kept != rows_now, None, {}
        held = dict((str(k), str(v)) for k, v in held.items())
        bodies_kept = kept.get("blocks") if isinstance(kept.get("blocks"), dict) else {}
        bodies_kept = dict((str(k), str(v)) for k, v in bodies_kept.items())
        return view, None, rows_kept != rows_now or held != slots, held, bodies_kept
    record = {"epoch": epoch, "rows": rows_now}
    if slots is not None:
        record["slots"] = slots
        if bodies:
            # Only with a held slot: without one the record is the one of before.
            record["blocks"] = bodies
    return st, canonical(record), False, None, {}


def target_reads(lg, cid):
    """The keys of the family out of the range read `cid` as state; a read
    that came back full is said, its last keys may be missing."""
    got = rows(lg, cid)
    fam = dict((str(r.get("key") or ""), str(r.get("value") or "")) for r in got
               if str(r.get("key") or "").startswith(CATALOG_KEY))
    if len(fam) >= TARGET_READ:
        sys.stderr.write("curator/policy: the range read of the targets came back full (%d"
                         " keys) -- a target past it is cut as unheard\n" % TARGET_READ)
    return fam


def cut_budget(target, st, frozen=None):
    """The budget of a call to `target` (GH #1450 Z1.7), one object every
    reader takes its number from: `soft`/`hard` -- a call that kept its
    turn's system keeps that system's window; else the row the target
    reported (`catalog:<target>`, before the tap's copy of it,
    OR-d38-3.c3b.5); else what the target's answers said
    (`catalog:<target>:input_soft`), else the wall's (`input_soft`) --,
    `line` the hard limit the call is guarded at, the fallback row's when
    none is known (GH #1225, K-3), `rate` the row's `chars_per_token`, else
    the tap's (0 when neither knows one), `target` the role's WINDOW_TARGET.
    The row is read field by field (review o15-R1 M4): a field it lacks is
    the tap's; its `input_soft` is cut to the window the target's own model
    reported (`catalog:<target>:context_window`); a target that never
    reported one is not cut. A reported row stands before every fallback
    knob (contract point 5)."""
    row = catalog_row(target, st)
    with_row = bool(cw_int(row.get("input_soft")))
    tap_soft = st.get(target_key(target, "input_soft"), "") or st.get("input_soft", "")
    tap_hard = st.get(target_key(target, "input_hard"), "") or st.get("input_hard", "")
    if frozen is not None:
        soft, hard = frozen["soft"], frozen["hard"]
    elif with_row:
        soft, hard = cw_int(row.get("input_soft")), row.get("input_hard") or tap_hard
        usable = cw_of(st.get(target_key(target, "context_window")))
        if usable > 0:
            soft = min(soft, usable)
    else:
        soft, hard = tap_soft, tap_hard
    return {"soft": soft, "hard": hard,
            "line": cw_int(hard) or int(FALLBACK_LIMITS.get("input_hard") or 0),
            "rate": (rate_of(row.get("chars_per_token")) if with_row else 0)
            or rate_of(st.get("chars_per_token")),
            "target": WINDOW_TARGET}


def system_mode(profile, way):
    """How a call sends its system part (contract point 3, field `system`):
    `delta` (the target holds its tree: the families that moved), `full`
    (the whole tree, and every delta target's sent state is cleared) or
    `none`. The profile's word wins; without one, a call that leaves the
    composite sends none and any other call holds the tree, as a bare
    curator does."""
    mode = str((profile or {}).get("system") or "") if isinstance(profile, dict) else ""
    if mode in ("delta", "full", "none"):
        return mode
    return "none" if way == "away" else "delta"


# D58 target (contract point 3, R-58-15): the profile a target's
# cell reported says how its calls are cut. A field it does not name takes
# its shipped value here; a window value it does not name takes the knob set
# on this instance, else that knob's shipped value -- the profile first, the
# instance second (contract point 3, "precedence"). The values a call's cut
# reads are the call's (`CALL_VALUES`); the wall's values the tap and the
# rebuild read stay the instance's (Nachtrag 11.11.).
PROFILE_SHIPPED = {"window": "wall", "system": "full", "tools": "all", "allow": [],
                   "must_call": False, "speaks": True, "instructions": {}, "frame": False,
                   "closes_turn": True, "recall": True, "feed_own": "renew"}
CALL_VALUES = ("keep_recent", "notes_share", "short_ids", "identity_budget", "state_lines",
               "broadcast_mode", "window_target")
ROLE_KEYS = tuple(SHIPPED)


def profile_held(target, st):
    """The profile the cell `target` reported beside its row, {} for none."""
    v = catalog_row(target, st).get("window_profile")
    return v if isinstance(v, dict) and v else {}


# Contract point 4: a call that leaves the composite has no cell here and no
# profile; the verdict says it departs, and this bundle goes with it -- no
# system part, no tool, no notes, it does not speak and does not end the turn.
DEPARTURE = {"system": "none", "tools": "none", "speaks": False, "closes_turn": False}


def flag_word(v):
    if isinstance(v, bool):
        return v
    return str(v).strip().lower() not in ("", "0", "false", "off", "no", "none")


def profile_params(profile, reported):
    """The knobs a cut reads, as `params` of the knob readers: a reported
    profile's value, else the instance's set knob, else the shipped value
    (`SHIPPED`); without a reported profile the instance's knobs."""
    if not reported:
        return dict(P)
    return dict((k, profile[k] if not unset(profile.get(k)) else P.get(k)) for k in ROLE_KEYS)


def call_profile(target, way, st):
    """The fields and the call's values of a call to `target` on `way` (the
    way only says whether the call leaves the composite, "away"). A target
    that reported no profile is cut with the shipped fields, holding its
    tree, and the instance's values (contract points 1 and 5)."""
    held = profile_held(target, st)
    reported = bool(held) and way != "away"
    base = held if reported else (DEPARTURE if way == "away" else {})
    cp = dict(PROFILE_SHIPPED)
    for f in PROFILE_SHIPPED:
        if f in base and base[f] is not None:
            cp[f] = base[f]
    for f in ("must_call", "speaks", "frame", "closes_turn", "recall"):
        cp[f] = flag_word(cp[f])
    cp["system"] = system_mode(base, way) if not reported else (
        cp["system"] if cp["system"] in ("delta", "full", "none") else "full")
    cp["window"] = "turn" if str(cp["window"]) == "turn" else "wall"
    cp["tools"] = cp["tools"] if cp["tools"] in ("all", "scoped", "none") else "all"
    cp["allow"] = names_list(cp["allow"])
    ins = cp["instructions"] if isinstance(cp["instructions"], dict) else {}
    cp["slot"] = str(ins.get("slot") or "").strip()
    cp["text"] = str(ins.get("text") or "")
    cp["only"] = flag_word(ins.get("only") or False)
    # D58 moveout (OR-d58-2.moveout.3, orchestrator ruling b): the slot a
    # side call to this target takes its text under (`instructions.<side_slot>`)
    # -- the target's profile names it, the curator holds no name of its own:
    # "" for a target that reported none (no side call goes to it).
    cp["side_slot"] = str(ins.get("side_slot") or "").strip()
    prm = profile_params(base, reported)
    if way == "away":
        # Contract point 4: a call that leaves the composite has no profile;
        # it is cut on the wall, so its call's values are the wall's -- the
        # one reported target that holds its tree, else the instance.
        holders = [t for t in held_targets(st)
                   if str(profile_held(t, st).get("system") or "") == "delta"]
        if len(holders) == 1:
            prm = profile_params(profile_held(holders[0], st), True)
    cp["short_window"] = "keep_recent" in base and cp["system"] != "delta"
    cp["keep_recent"] = int(number_of(prm, "keep_recent"))
    cp["notes_share"] = max(0.0, number_of(prm, "notes_share"))
    cp["short_ids"] = flag_of(prm, "short_ids")
    cp["identity_budget"] = identity_budget_of(prm)
    cp["state_lines"] = max(0, int(number_of(prm, "state_lines")))
    cp["broadcast_mode"] = str(knob_of(prm, "broadcast_mode")).strip()
    cp["window_target"] = max(0, int(number_of(prm, "window_target")))
    cp["reported"] = reported
    return cp


# D58 target (plan part, Nachtrag 11.11. Nr. 1 to 3): the wall belongs to
# every target of the curator at once, so a value the tap of an answer or a
# rebuild reads has one source -- the target that holds its tree (`system`
# `delta`): the call's own when it does, else the one reported target that
# does. None or several, and the call goes to none of them: the knobs of the
# instance, and a mark (`target_unknown`, `missing` "wall",
# OR-d58-2.target.6) when some target reported a profile; a curator no cell
# reported a profile to runs on its instance as before, unmarked. The
# values a call's cut reads stay the call's (`call_profile`).
WALL_VALUES = ("keep_recent", "keep_recent_tokens", "compress_at", "rebuild_to", "horizon",
               "tiers", "keep_rounds", "gc", "gc_scaffold", "stub_tools_after", "window_target",
               "state_lines")


def wall_source(target, cp, st):
    """`(target, profile, unknown)` of the wall for a call to `target` cut
    by `cp`: the tree-holding target ("" for none), the profile it reported
    ({} for none: the instance's knobs) and whether the wall had no source
    although a target reported a profile. Bauer 5 calls it for the row of
    the rebuild and the self-summary."""
    if target and cp["system"] == "delta":
        return target, (profile_held(target, st) if cp["reported"] else {}), False
    reported = [t for t in held_targets(st) if profile_held(t, st)]
    holders = [t for t in reported if str(profile_held(t, st).get("system") or "") == "delta"]
    if len(holders) == 1:
        return holders[0], profile_held(holders[0], st), False
    return "", {}, bool(reported)


def wall_values(profile):
    """The wall's values in the order of `WALL_VALUES` out of the reported
    `profile` of the tree-holding target: its value, else the knob set on
    the instance, else the shipped value (`profile_params`) -- read like
    the module's own values of the instance."""
    prm = profile_params(profile, True)
    return (int(number_of(prm, "keep_recent")),
            0 if unset(knob_of(prm, "keep_recent_tokens"))
            else max(0, int(number_of(prm, "keep_recent_tokens"))),
            number_of(prm, "compress_at"), number_of(prm, "rebuild_to"), horizon_of(prm),
            tiers_of(prm), int(number_of(prm, "keep_rounds")), switch_on(knob_of(prm, "gc")),
            switch_on(knob_of(prm, "gc_scaffold")), int(number_of(prm, "stub_tools_after")),
            max(0, int(number_of(prm, "window_target"))),
            max(0, int(number_of(prm, "state_lines"))))


def claim_wall(info):
    """The tree-holding target's profile a rebuild's claim carries (`wall`,
    phase `rb-probe`), {} for none: the instance's values then."""
    w = info.get("wall") if isinstance(info, dict) else None
    prof = w.get("profile") if isinstance(w, dict) else None
    return prof if isinstance(prof, dict) else {}


def slot_path(slot):
    return "instructions." + slot if slot else ""


def foreign_slots(cp, st):
    """The instruction slots other targets name -- a target reads the family
    `instructions` without them (contract point 3, `instructions`)."""
    held = dict((t, profile_held(t, st)) for t in held_targets(st))
    names = set(str((p.get("instructions") if isinstance(p.get("instructions"), dict) else {})
                    .get("slot") or "").strip() for p in held.values())
    names.discard("")
    names.discard(cp["slot"])
    return [slot_path(n) for n in sorted(names)]


def without_slots(leaves, paths):
    return [x for x in leaves
            if not any(x[0] == q or x[0].startswith(q + ".") for q in paths)]


def own_slot_leaves(leaves, cp):
    """With the target's own slot among the leaves and its profile's
    `instructions.only` on, the other leaves of `instructions` go, except
    the sidecar contract and the session's own slots; without `only` the
    family stays and the slot stands beside it (contract point 3,
    OR-d58-2.target.50, .53)."""
    q = slot_path(cp["slot"])
    has = bool(q) and any(x[0] == q or x[0].startswith(q + ".") for x in leaves)
    if not cp["only"] or not has:
        return leaves
    return [x for x in leaves if not in_family(x[0], "instructions")
            or x[0] == q or x[0].startswith(q + ".")
            or in_family(x[0], CONTRACT_PATH) or session_bound(x[0])]


def system_ordered(leaves, order):
    """The leaves of the system part in the order the target's cell lays
    them before the provider: the families of `order` first, as listed, then
    the rest alphabetically; within a family as they stand. The entry "*"
    stands for that rest: the families listed after it come after the rest,
    as listed (GH #1478; the cell refuses a second "*"). A family listed
    twice takes its first place, as in the cell."""
    order = [str(f) for f in (order or []) if isinstance(f, str)]
    rest = order.index("*") if "*" in order else len(order)
    rank = {}
    for i, f in enumerate(order):
        if f != "*" and f not in rank:
            rank[f] = i

    def place(x):
        family = x[0].split(".")[0]
        if family not in rank:
            return (1, 0, family)
        return (0 if rank[family] < rest else 2, rank[family], "")
    return sorted(leaves, key=place)


# >>> cut v1 (GH #1450, D38 C3b, R-38-4 Nr. 3/5)
# STAGE 2: THE CUT OF ONE CALL. Stage 1 (the plan) is model-free; the cut
# takes the call's blocks to its target's window -- the catalogue row of the
# target cell, else the window known so far -- and never adds one: every id
# it sends is one of the call's blocks, every block it leaves out it names
# with its reason. Pure: no ledger op, no state, the one clock its own
# station time (`cut_ms`, monotonic). The wire (cache breakpoints, dialect)
# stays the llm cell's; `cache_at` is the boundary of the stable prefix --
# the last block before the running round -- for the snapshot only
# (OR-d38-3.c3b.3).
def cut_timed(spent, fn, *args):
    """`fn(*args)`, its time added to `spent[0]` (seconds): `cut_ms` is the
    sum of the cut's own functions, nothing of `win` between them (review
    o15-R1 M5)."""
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    try:
        return fn(*args)
    finally:
        spent[0] += time.perf_counter() - t0


def cut(blocks, wall, stages, row, target, budget, current, spent, tools=None):
    """The cut of a call as a record: `blocks` the call's blocks in their
    order, `wall` its wall rows, `stages` the wall positions the window held
    after the render, the hard guard and the way's scope, `row` the target's
    catalogue row ({} without one), `budget` `{soft, target, hard}`,
    `current` the running round `(session_id, turn_id)`, `spent` the
    seconds the cut's other functions took (`cut_timed`), `tools` the names
    the call's tool scope allows (None: no scope). `stages[3]`, when given,
    is the order the wall positions are sent in (after `ambient_first`):
    `ids` and `cache_at` follow it (review o15-R1 M1)."""
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    seq_hash, cur = {}, set()
    for r in wall or []:
        if isinstance(r, dict):
            h = str(r.get("hash") or "") or block_hash(element_of(r) or {})
            seq_hash[int(r.get("seq") or 0)] = h
            if (str(r.get("session_id") or ""), str(r.get("turn_id") or "")) == tuple(current):
                cur.add(h)
    rendered, guarded, scoped = (set(seq_hash[p] for p in st if p in seq_hash)
                                 for st in stages[:3])
    ids, dropped, seen, cur_ids = [], [], set(), set()
    for b in blocks:
        bid, o = str(b.get("id") or ""), b.get("origin") or {}
        if bid in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(bid)
        if o.get("source") == "wall":
            h = str(o.get("hash") or "")
            if h not in scoped:
                dropped.append({"id": bid, "why": "quick_scope" if h in guarded
                                else "overflow_cut" if h in rendered else "not_shown"})
                continue
            if h in cur:
                cur_ids.add(bid)
        ids.append(bid)
    if len(stages) > 3:
        # The wall blocks in the order they are sent; the others keep their
        # place (the system part and the identity stand before the wall).
        rank = {}
        for i, p in enumerate(stages[3]):
            rank.setdefault(seq_hash.get(p), i)
        wall_of = dict((str(b.get("id") or ""), str((b.get("origin") or {}).get("hash") or ""))
                       for b in blocks if (b.get("origin") or {}).get("source") == "wall")
        sent = iter(sorted((bid for bid in ids if bid in wall_of),
                           key=lambda bid: rank.get(wall_of[bid], len(rank))))
        ids = [next(sent) if bid in wall_of else bid for bid in ids]
    mode = row.get("cache_mode") or None
    cache_at = None
    if mode not in (None, "none"):
        before = []
        for bid in ids:
            if bid in cur_ids:
                break
            before.append(bid)
        cache_at = before[-1] if before else None
    return {"target": target, "model": row.get("model") or None, "ids": ids,
            "dropped": dropped, "budget": budget, "cache_mode": mode,
            "cache_ttl_s": row.get("cache_ttl_s"), "cache_at": cache_at, "tools": tools,
            "cut_ms": round((spent[0] + time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000.0, 3)}


def sent_add(out, puts, value, kind, form, store, carried=None):
    """One entry of `sent` (GH #1462) for `value` as it was sent: `hash` the
    sha256 of its canonical JSON -- the block of the ledger that holds these
    bytes --, `kind`, `form` and `bytes`, the length of that JSON in UTF-8.
    `puts` gets the block `(hash, store, chars, body)` for `sent_ops`; `store`
    is the kind its row in `blocks` takes when the ledger does not hold it.
    An entry of the system part says `carried` (a bool, see `sent_list`); any
    other entry has no such key."""
    body = canonical(value)
    raw = body.encode("utf-8")
    h = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
    out.append({"hash": h, "kind": kind, "form": form, "bytes": len(raw)})
    if carried is not None:
        out[-1]["carried"] = bool(carried)
    text = value.get("text") if isinstance(value, dict) else None
    puts.append((h, store, len(text) if isinstance(text, str) else len(body), body))


def sent_kinds(blocks, wall):
    """The kind of the plan's block at each wall position (GH #1462): the
    blocks of the wall in `blocks` by their origin hash, the positions as
    `cut` reads them off `wall`."""
    by_hash = dict((str((b.get("origin") or {}).get("hash") or ""), str(b.get("kind") or ""))
                   for b in blocks if (b.get("origin") or {}).get("source") == "wall")
    out = {}
    for r in wall or []:
        if isinstance(r, dict):
            h = str(r.get("hash") or "") or block_hash(element_of(r) or {})
            if by_hash.get(h):
                out[int(r.get("seq") or 0)] = by_hash[h]
    return out


def sent_list(leaves, system, built, head_el, msgs, lead, pieces, tools, order=None):
    """What a call sent, as the list `sent` of its snapshot row (GH #1462,
    R-38-4 Nr. 5) and the blocks that hold its bytes: `(entries, puts)`.

    The order is the order sent: the leaves of the system part `leaves`
    (`(path, text, hash)`; a path in `built` was made by the cut and is held
    by no slot), the identity `head_el` (None: none), the messages `msgs` as
    `(element, kind, form)`, and the tool menu `tools` (the scope's menu
    part, `scope_menu`; None: the call names no scope).

    The system part is read off `system`, the tree the cut SENT with this
    call (the families that moved, each whole): the model's cell holds the
    rest from the calls before, so every leaf of `leaves` is listed -- the
    whole tree the model holds for this call -- and says `carried`: true for
    a leaf of a family in `system`, the bytes this call carried, false for one
    the model's cell held already. A first call carries all of them. A call
    whose cut sent no system part at all leaves its target under the target's
    own and lists no leaf. Nothing here asks which way or which cell the call
    took: the list follows what the cut handed it.

    `pieces` are the lines of the
    notes block `lead` as `(kind, element)`: they are made in the cut and
    sent INSIDE the message that carries the block, so each stands as an
    entry of its own (form `built`) right before that message, and the
    message stands whole behind them -- the bytes of the pieces are part of
    its bytes (OR-d58-2.snap.3). A block the call did not send (its carrier
    left the window) lists no piece; an element that is the notes block alone
    (no words of the person in the window) is a note, built. Pure: it reads
    nothing, the caller hands what the cut already holds.

    `order` is the order of the system part the target's cell reported
    (D58 target, contract point 2): its families first, then the rest
    alphabetically, as the cell lays them; None (no reported row) keeps
    the leaves by path."""
    out, puts = [], []
    if order is not None:
        leaves = system_ordered(leaves, order)
    for path, text, _ in (leaves if system else []):
        sent_add(out, puts, {"path": path, "text": text}, "frame",
                 "built" if path in built else "raw", "system",
                 path.split(".")[0] in system)
    if head_el is not None:
        sent_add(out, puts, head_el, "frame", "raw", IDENTITY_FULL_KIND)
    at = None
    if lead and pieces:
        for i, (el, _, _) in enumerate(msgs):
            if el.get("origin") == "user" and lead in str(el.get("text") or ""):
                at = i
    for i, (el, kind, form) in enumerate(msgs):
        if i == at:
            for p_kind, p_el in pieces:
                sent_add(out, puts, p_el, p_kind, "built", "view")
        if lead and el.get("text") == lead:
            kind, form = "note", "built"
        sent_add(out, puts, el, kind, form, "view")
    if tools is not None:
        sent_add(out, puts, tools, "tools", "raw", "view")
    return out, puts


# GH #1463 (D58 form, R-58-8): what `window_lost` watches -- an element the
# model must keep in view. One rule per block kind, the same for every role:
# the person's words, an answer, a tool result that failed, and the outcome
# of an errand that ended without an answer (GH #1469, kind `outcome`).
LOST_KINDS = ("words", "answer", "outcome")
# The verdicts of the watch a call hands its tap (`window_est:<call>`).
WATCH_FIELDS = ("prefix_break", "window_lost")


def sent_parts(sent):
    """`(system, messages)` of a `sent` list (GH #1463): the hashes of the
    system part -- EVERY entry of the tree the model holds, never only the
    carried ones --, sorted, and the entries of the messages in the order
    sent (the pieces of the notes block among them; their bytes are part of
    the element behind them). An entry with `why` was not sent, the tool
    menu is no message."""
    sent = [e for e in sent if isinstance(e, dict)]
    return (sorted(str(e.get("hash") or "") for e in sent if "carried" in e),
            [e for e in sent
             if "carried" not in e and "why" not in e and e.get("kind") != "tools"])


def sent_menu(sent):
    """The hash of the tool menu a `sent` list names (its `tools` entry,
    GH #1497), "" when the call named no scope."""
    return next((str(e.get("hash") or "") for e in sent or []
                 if isinstance(e, dict) and e.get("kind") == "tools"), "")


def window_watch(prev_sent, prev_round, now_sent, now_round, placed, sent_seqs, cover,
                 failed, rebuilt, held=None):
    """The two verdicts of a call on its own window (GH #1463), read off the
    `sent` list of the call before it to the same target (`prev_sent`) and
    its own (`now_sent`): `{"prefix_break": 0|1, "window_lost": n}`.

    `prev_round`/`now_round` are the running rounds `(session_id, turn_id)`
    of the two calls; `placed` maps the hash of a wall row this call read to
    its `(seq, round)` places; `sent_seqs` the wall positions this call
    sends; `cover` the plan's cover; `failed(hash)` says whether the wall
    block is a tool result that failed; `rebuilt` that a rebuild or the
    guard at the hard line lay between the two calls.

    PREFIX (contract point 7, OR-58-63). Within a round the call begins with
    the WHOLE window before it. Across the round boundary it begins with
    that window up to its running round -- the place the model cell's second
    cache mark stood at; what lay behind it was never in a cached prefix.
    The system part is the same tree. After a rebuild there is no verdict:
    the rebuild is the one place a prefix may change.

    HELD (GH #1497). The tree a call is judged against is the one the
    target HOLDS: the system part of the newest earlier call to it that
    listed one (`held`, a `sent` list; None: the call before). A call that
    sends no system part (a consult) lists none and leaves the tree as it
    was; compared only when both listed one, the call after such a call was
    never judged, and a leaf that joined the tree there went unseen -- only
    one that left was counted (probe-10 of the strand: `consult.pending`
    came after the consult unseen and was counted when it went). A leaf that
    comes and a leaf that goes are both a break. The tool menu the target
    holds is judged the same way (`sent_menu`, review I2 of the strand): the
    provider sends it before the system part, so a menu that changes without
    a rebuild -- a scope that comes, goes or names other tools -- is a break
    as well (probe-10 of the strand, t3: a running consult's `deny` joined
    the scope of the speaking call and left with the advice; the watch, which
    judged no menu, counted neither).

    LOST (R-58-8). An element of `LOST_KINDS` or a failed tool result that
    the window before sent as it stands in the wall, that lies above the
    cover (no summary holds it) and that this call sends in no form. An
    element whose bytes the cut made (the words under the notes block, a
    stub) names no wall row and is not judged; one left out with a reason
    is a recall block and none of these kinds. Pure."""
    p_sys, p_msgs = sent_parts(prev_sent)
    n_sys, n_msgs = sent_parts(now_sent)
    h_sys = sent_parts(held)[0] if held is not None else p_sys
    h_menu = sent_menu(held if held is not None else prev_sent)
    p_hash = [str(e.get("hash") or "") for e in p_msgs]
    n_hash = [str(e.get("hash") or "") for e in n_msgs]
    brk = 0
    if not rebuilt:
        n = len(p_msgs)
        if tuple(prev_round) != tuple(now_round):
            # By place, not by content (form review M-1): of the occurrences
            # of one hash in the window before, the last ones are the running
            # round's -- as many as the round holds places of it; an earlier
            # one with the same content lies before the round.
            total, seen = {}, {}
            for h in p_hash:
                total[h] = total.get(h, 0) + 1
            for i, e in enumerate(p_msgs):
                h = p_hash[i]
                inside = sum(1 for _, rnd in placed.get(h, ())
                             if tuple(rnd) == tuple(prev_round))
                nth = seen.get(h, 0)
                seen[h] = nth + 1
                if e.get("form") == "built" or nth >= total[h] - inside:
                    n = i
                    break
        if (h_sys and n_sys and (h_sys != n_sys or h_menu != sent_menu(now_sent))) \
                or n_hash[:n] != p_hash[:n]:
            brk = 1
    lost, held = 0, set(n_hash)
    for e, h in zip(p_msgs, p_hash):
        if e.get("form") != "raw" or h in held:
            continue
        kind = str(e.get("kind") or "")
        if kind not in LOST_KINDS and not (kind == "tool_result" and failed(h)):
            continue
        spots = placed.get(h)
        if not spots or any(seq in sent_seqs for seq, _ in spots) \
                or all(seq <= cover for seq, _ in spots):
            continue
        lost += 1
    return {"prefix_break": brk, "window_lost": lost}


def cut_items(items, wall, plan, fixed, head_el, cp, line, current, lead, own, drop=None,
              legend=None):
    """The rules of the target over the rendered items of a call, in their
    order (GH #1450 Z1.5): the guard at HARD_HEADROOM of the line `line`
    (`guard_cut`, the oldest whole rounds, GH #1225), then the quick way's
    scope (`quick_items`, GH #1347), then order and frame (Z1.6, R-38-4
    Nr. 3: they move and format, they leave nothing out). Returns the items
    to send, the items before the order (`unmoved`, a side call filters them
    itself), the guard's `overflow` record (None under the line) and the
    wall positions after each stage for `cut`. `fixed`/`head_el` are the
    system leaves and the identity the estimate counts beside the items;
    `lead` the notes block's text, `own` the person's own words. `drop`
    (D38 V5, None when off) maps the positions the guard and the quick
    filter kept to the positions that leave before the order. `legend`
    (GH #1471) is the session boundary the turn of the call keeps
    (`turn_legend`), None for a turn that keeps none."""
    stages = [[it[0] for it in items]]
    whole = estimate_tokens({"system": fixed,
                             "messages": head_el + [el for _, el, _, _ in items]})
    overflow = None
    if line > 0 and whole >= HARD_HEADROOM * line:
        items, gone = guard_cut(items, wall, plan_cover(plan, []) if plan else 0,
                                lambda els: estimate_tokens({"system": fixed,
                                                             "messages": head_el + els}),
                                HARD_HEADROOM * line)
        after = estimate_tokens({"system": fixed,
                                 "messages": head_el + [el for _, el, _, _ in items]})
        overflow = {"before": whole, "after": after,
                    "limit": int(HARD_HEADROOM * line), "rounds": len(gone),
                    "from_seq": min([s for g in gone for s in g] or [0]),
                    "to_seq": max([s for g in gone for s in g] or [0])}
    stages.append([it[0] for it in items])
    if cp["short_window"]:
        items = quick_items(items, wall, cp["keep_recent"], current, not cp["recall"])
    elif not cp["recall"]:
        items = quick_items(items, wall, 0, current, True)
    if cp["window"] == "turn":
        t_keep = set(id(el) for el in turn_window([el for _, el, _, _ in items]))
        items = [it for it in items if id(it[1]) in t_keep]
    stages.append([it[0] for it in items])
    if drop is not None:
        # D38 V5 (review d38_o28-R1 M1, pin gh_d38_pins_c): the recall pairs
        # leave here, behind the guard and BEFORE the order -- `ambient_first`
        # folds a pair of the oldest sent round into the person's words, and
        # dropped behind it the folded quote went twice while the snapshot
        # and the hop named it dropped.
        gone = drop(set(it[0] for it in items))
        if gone:
            items = [it for it in items if it[0] not in gone]
            stages = [[p for p in st if p not in gone] for st in stages]
    # GH #1333 (review I-1/I-2): the ambient pairs move last, on what is sent
    # -- after the guard's cut and the quick filter, so the request still
    # opens with the person's words and the quick way never sees a recall.
    # A side call filters the unmoved items itself.
    unmoved = items
    keys = round_keys(wall)
    items = ambient_first(items, keys, lead)
    # GH #1335: the session boundary, last and on what is sent -- text only.
    items = session_bounds(items, keys, current[0], session_spans(wall), lead, legend)
    # GH #1337: the person's words framed, last -- text only.
    items = person_frame(items, own, keys, tuple(current), SHORT_IDS)
    stages.append([it[0] for it in items])
    return items, unmoved, overflow, stages


def cut_side(unmoved, wall, window, current, keep):
    """The window of a side call (GH #1248), cut where every call is cut
    (review o15-R1 I3): the scope of a short window over the items before
    the order (`quick_items`), no lookups -- a result of an earlier turn is
    content it could repeat as this one's (GH #1260, OR-WG-9, B-L3) --, on
    the entry's `window` `turn` the person's turn alone (`side_window`).
    Returns the messages and the wall positions they come from."""
    b_items = quick_items(unmoved, wall, keep, current)
    b_items = [it for it in b_items
               if str(it[1].get("type") or "") not in ("tool_call", "tool_result")]
    msgs = side_window(window, [el for _, el, _, _ in b_items])
    kept = set(id(el) for el in msgs)
    return msgs, [p for p, el, _, _ in b_items if id(el) in kept]


def cut_tools(cp, spec, scope, spec_tools, families, folded, offered, needs, it_now):
    """The tool scope of the quick way's target (GH #1450 Z1.8) and whether
    the call is its tool round: the spec call sees `spec_tools` only, never
    a tool round (GH #1275); a quick call the families' scope (`quick_scope`)
    and, when its stamp needs a tool with no result in the round yet and a
    tool left to call, the required tool round (GH #1260, OR-WG-6: the fast
    model called its tool in 0 of 5 lab turns and 7 of 10 probe calls, 10 of
    10 only when required, lab BL1). Every other way: (None, False)."""
    if spec:
        return spec_cut(scope, spec_tools, folded, offered), False
    if cp["tools"] != "scoped":
        return None, (cp["must_call"] and cp["tools"] == "all" and "tool" in needs
                      and it_now < 1 and bool(offered))
    q = quick_scope(families, scope, folded, offered, cp["allow"])
    tool_round = cp["must_call"] and "tool" in needs and it_now < 1 and bool(q.get("allow"))
    if tool_round:
        q["require"] = True
    return q, tool_round


def cut_scope(cp, slim, q_scope, no_tools, deny, spec=False, tool_round=False):
    """The `tool_scope` the call sends (GH #1450 Z1.8) as (present, scope,
    refused): the plan's on a brain call, the quick way's own on a quick
    call, none on every other way; a turn whose class entry says `tools`
    "none" gets no tool at any target, nothing opened (GH #1279, #1478).
    While the session's consult runs no speaking call can start another one
    (`deny`, the names the lead denies, GH #1280/#1447) -- since GH #1497 not
    by the menu but at the call: `refused` names what the deny would have
    taken off this call's menu, the call carries it as `hop.tools_refused`,
    and the composite's dispatcher answers such a call with a tool error
    instead of running it.
    The menu stays as it was: the provider sends it before the system part,
    and a deny that came with the consult and went with the advice changed
    the front of the window twice without a rebuild (review I2 of the
    strand, probe-10 t3)."""
    has, scope = "tool_scope" in slim, slim.get("tool_scope")
    if cp["tools"] == "scoped" or spec:
        has, scope = True, q_scope
    elif cp["tools"] == "none":
        # A reported `none`: the cell offers no tool; a call that leaves the
        # composition sends no scope, as before.
        has, scope = (True, {"allow": []}) if cp["reported"] else (False, None)
    elif tool_round:
        has, scope = True, dict(scope if isinstance(scope, dict) else {}, require=True)
    if no_tools:
        has, scope = True, no_tool_scope(scope)
    refused = []
    if deny and cp["speaks"]:
        have = names_list(scope.get("deny")) if isinstance(scope, dict) else []
        d_scope = with_deny(scope, names_list(deny))
        refused = [n for n in (names_list(d_scope.get("deny"))
                               if isinstance(d_scope, dict) else []) if n not in have]
    return has, scope, refused


def scope_names(scope):
    """The tool names a scope allows, for the snapshot; None = no scope."""
    if not isinstance(scope, dict) or not isinstance(scope.get("allow"), list):
        return None
    return [str(x) for x in scope["allow"]]


def scope_menu(scope):
    """The part of a call's `tool_scope` that makes the menu the model is
    sent, as the `tools` entry of `sent` (GH #1497): `allow` when the scope
    names one, `deny` and `hint` when not empty; None = the call names no
    scope (the target's whole menu). The provider puts the menu before the
    system part, so a menu that changes breaks the cached prefix like a
    system part that changes -- a `deny` alone (no `allow`) changed it
    unseen. `require` asks for a call and leaves the menu as it is."""
    if not isinstance(scope, dict):
        return None
    out = {}
    if isinstance(scope.get("allow"), list):
        out["allow"] = [str(x) for x in scope["allow"]]
    for k in ("deny", "hint"):
        if names_list(scope.get(k)):
            out[k] = names_list(scope.get(k))
    return out


def cut_system(leaves, sent, mode, slots_failed):
    """The system part a call sends for its target (GH #1450 Z1.9) as
    (system, fams, changed, removed, clear_sent): the families whose hash
    moved against `sent` (the policy's `system_hash_sent`), the gated and
    the session families whole on every call, a quick call its whole tree,
    a consult none; `clear_sent` = the caller clears `system_hash_sent`
    (the state stays the policy's, the cut is pure)."""
    fams = family_hashes(leaves)
    changed = sorted(f for f in fams if sent.get(f) != fams[f])
    removed = sorted(f for f in sent if f not in fams)
    if slots_failed:
        # The slots are unknown, not gone: the model keeps the families it
        # holds; only the gated ones go whole below, as on every call.
        changed, removed = [], []
    system, clear_sent = {}, False
    for f in changed:
        system[f] = family_node(f, leaves)
    for f in removed:
        system[f] = {"$replace": True}
    # THE GATED FAMILIES GO WHOLE, ON EVERY CALL (GH #925, review I-2). The
    # model's `llm` keeps ONE system tree, and it answers a call with what
    # that call's message left in it. Two calls of two rounds overlap (two
    # channels of one brain): each reads `system_hash_sent` before the
    # other's `done` lands, so a diff against it lets A's leaf -- a summary
    # only A's round may see -- stand when B is answered. A state keyed per
    # round alone would not close that: B still reads it before A writes it.
    # So the families that carry rows of other rounds are sent in every call
    # as their whole `$replace` root, empty when the round sees nothing; the
    # same leaves are the same text, so the provider's prefix cache stays.
    # The families that hold a session's slots go whole for the same reason
    # (review I-4): the `llm` keeps the legend, the consults and the peer rule
    # of whichever call came last, so each call sends its own, empty included.
    # The other families hold neither and keep the diff.
    for f in GATED_FAMILIES + SESSION_FAMILIES:
        system[f] = family_node(f, leaves)
    if mode != "delta":
        # GH #1247: the quick window goes whole (a model of its own, or the
        # brain without the contract), and `system_hash_sent` is cleared so the
        # brain's next call sends its whole tree again; a consult carries no
        # system part -- cogny answers under its own.
        system = {f: family_node(f, leaves) for f in fams} if mode == "full" else {}
        changed, removed = [], []
        if mode == "full":
            # Re-check I1 (the class of GH #925): `./quick` is an `llm` of its
            # own and keeps ONE system tree too -- a family this call does not
            # name stands as the last call left it. Sent only with leaves, the
            # summary or the pin of one round stood for the quick turn of the
            # next. So the gated and the session families go whole here as
            # well, empty when the round sees nothing.
            for f in GATED_FAMILIES + SESSION_FAMILIES:
                system[f] = family_node(f, leaves)
            clear_sent = True
    return system, fams, changed, removed, clear_sent

def rebuild_to_of(limits):
    """The aim of a `soft` or `hard` rebuild in tokens, out of the package:
    `input_soft` times `rebuild_to` / `compress_at`. 0 = no aim (no soft
    limit, `rebuild_to` 0)."""
    soft = (limits or {}).get("input_soft", 0)
    if soft <= 0 or REBUILD_TO <= 0 or COMPRESS_AT <= 0:
        return 0
    return int(round(soft * REBUILD_TO / COMPRESS_AT))


def cost_aim_of(limits):
    """The aim of a `cost` rebuild in tokens: `input_soft` times `rebuild_to`
    (OR-HK-25). Lower than a soft rebuild's on purpose: with the soft share
    as its aim (talky 0.35 / 0.5 = 0.7 of soft) the rule fired only at a
    cached price above 23 % of the input price -- never at the usual 10 %
    (KF2 review B2); with this one it is due from 0.7 (talky, consult) or
    0.5 (coding, research) of soft at 10 % and ten turns. 0 = no aim."""
    soft = (limits or {}).get("input_soft", 0)
    if soft <= 0 or REBUILD_TO <= 0:
        return 0
    return int(round(soft * REBUILD_TO))


def step_of(tokens, limits):
    """The step of the price ladder a window of `tokens` falls in (GH
    #1431): the last step whose `above_input` `tokens` exceeds -- the base
    step (`above_input` 0) for any window above 0. {} without a ladder."""
    hit = {}
    if isinstance(tokens, bool) or not isinstance(tokens, (int, float)):
        return hit
    for s in (limits or {}).get("price_tiers") or []:
        if tokens > s.get("above_input", 0):
            hit = s
    return hit


def prices_of(tokens, limits):
    """`(cost_in, cost_cached_in)` for a window of `tokens`: its step's when
    a ladder is stamped (a step without a cached price reads at its input
    price, as the llm cell stamps it), else the stamped `cost_in` /
    `cost_cached_in` as before."""
    lim = limits or {}
    s = step_of(tokens, lim) or lim
    ci = s.get("cost_in", 0)
    return ci, s.get("cost_cached_in", ci)


def _turn_units(window, cached, limits):
    """`turn_cost` times 1e6 (tokens x cents per million): the cost rule
    floors a quotient of two of these, and a division by 1e6 before the floor
    could tip it by one at an exact bound (fix round 1, review M-1)."""
    if isinstance(window, bool) or not isinstance(window, (int, float)):
        return None
    ci, cc = prices_of(window, limits)
    if ci <= 0:
        return None
    c = cached if isinstance(cached, (int, float)) and not isinstance(cached, bool) else 0
    c = min(max(c, 0), window)
    return (window - c) * ci + c * cc


def turn_cost(window, cached, limits):
    """The input of one turn in cents (GH #1431): the fresh part at the
    input price, the cached part at the cached price, both of the step the
    window falls in -- the provider prices a request by all its input tokens,
    cache reads included. None without an input price or a window."""
    u = _turn_units(window, cached, limits)
    return None if u is None else u / 1e6


def write_price_of(tokens, limits):
    """The price of writing a rebuilt window of `tokens` into the cache
    (GH #1431): its step's `cost_cache_write`, else its step's input price --
    the rule of before counted the rebuild at `cost_in`."""
    lim = limits or {}
    w = (step_of(tokens, lim) or lim).get("cost_cache_write", 0)
    return w if w > 0 else prices_of(tokens, lim)[0]


def amortise_after(window, rebuild_to, cost_in, cost_cached_in, limits=None):
    """The turn on which one rebuild has paid for itself: keeping the window
    costs `(window - rebuild_to) * cost_cached_in` a turn more than the
    rebuilt one, the rebuild `rebuild_to * cost_in` once -- the smallest N
    with `(window - rebuild_to) * cost_cached_in * N > rebuild_to * cost_in`.
    None when keeping costs nothing more. With a price ladder in `limits`
    (GH #1431) each side is priced at its own step: the held and the rebuilt
    window, both cached, by `turn_cost`, and the rebuild at the cache-write
    price of the aim's step (`write_price_of`). Without one the rule of
    before, with the rebuild at the row's `cost_cache_write` when `limits`
    names one over 0 (GH #1464): a rebuild writes the whole rebuilt window
    into the cache, whatever the shape of the price list; a row without a
    write price, and the four-argument call, price it at `cost_in` as
    before."""
    lim = limits or {}
    if not lim.get("price_tiers"):
        keep = (window - rebuild_to) * cost_cached_in
        if keep <= 0:
            return None
        write = lim.get("cost_cache_write") or 0
        price = write if isinstance(write, (int, float)) and write > 0 else cost_in
        return int((rebuild_to * price) // keep) + 1
    held, rebuilt = _turn_units(window, window, limits), _turn_units(rebuild_to, rebuild_to, limits)
    if held is None or rebuilt is None or held - rebuilt <= 0:
        return None
    return int((rebuild_to * write_price_of(rebuild_to, limits)) // (held - rebuilt)) + 1


def target_aim_of(limits):
    """The aim of a `target` or `day` rebuild in tokens (GH #1272): the
    role's `window_target` times `rebuild_to` / `compress_at` -- the
    proportion a `soft` rebuild keeps to `input_soft` --, never above the
    aim of a `soft` rebuild when the package names one. 0 = no aim
    (`window_target` or `rebuild_to` 0)."""
    if WINDOW_TARGET <= 0 or REBUILD_TO <= 0 or COMPRESS_AT <= 0:
        return 0
    aim = int(round(WINDOW_TARGET * REBUILD_TO / COMPRESS_AT))
    rb = rebuild_to_of(limits)
    return min(aim, rb) if rb > 0 else aim


def cold_aim_of(inherited):
    """The aim of a rebuild after an expired cache in tokens (GH #1464,
    addendum 10.11.): with `cold_to` set, that share of the role's
    `window_target` -- a value of its own, whatever the package of the last
    answer says --, 0 for a role without a target (it only collects);
    without `cold_to`, `inherited`, the aim the order of the cache carried."""
    if COLD_TO is None:
        return int(inherited or 0)
    if WINDOW_TARGET <= 0:
        return 0
    return int(round(WINDOW_TARGET * COLD_TO))


def curate_mark(window, limits, n=None, next_estimate=0, day_due=False, target_at=0):
    """What a turn's window calls for, as `{mark, rebuild_to}`: `hard` over
    `input_hard` -- or when `next_estimate`, the llm cell's estimate of the
    next window, reaches HARD_HEADROOM of it --, `soft` at `input_soft`,
    `day` when the turn is on another UTC day than the last rebuild of a
    role with a day horizon (`day_due`, GH #1272), `target` at the role's
    `window_target` under soft (GH #1272), `cost` under soft when the cached
    rest over `n` turns (`amortise_turns`) costs more than one rebuild to
    the lower aim of `cost_aim_of` (then `rebuild_to` is that aim), else
    `none` -- and `none` without a window. Without a soft limit only `day`
    and `target` are read: the window, not the model, drives cost and
    latency (GH #1272); both aim at `target_aim_of`, or at the soft aim
    when the role has no target. `target_at` is the lowest window of the
    round since its last `target` order -- the window the rebuild left --
    while the window stayed over the target since: then `target` waits until
    the window has grown by `window_target` - the aim from there (reviews
    I-1, I-3, GH #1272) -- a rebuild that kept the window over the
    target with the rounds it keeps raw would condense next to nothing on
    every turn and break the cache each time; the mark is then `none` with
    `hold` = `target_at`. With a price ladder on the tap (GH #1431, R-38-2
    "UX before price") `cost` never fires while the window is at or under
    the role's `window_target` or held over it: the target sets the size of
    the window, not the price -- a `cost` rebuild in the hold would order the
    aim the `target` rebuild just missed on every turn (fix round 1, I-1)."""
    n = AMORTISE_TURNS if n is None else n
    lim = limits or {}
    rb = rebuild_to_of(lim)
    soft = lim.get("input_soft", 0)
    if isinstance(window, bool) or not isinstance(window, (int, float)):
        return {"mark": "none", "rebuild_to": rb}
    ta = target_aim_of(lim)
    target_due = WINDOW_TARGET > 0 and window >= WINDOW_TARGET and (soft <= 0 or window < soft)
    held = target_due and isinstance(target_at, (int, float)) and target_at > 0 \
        and window < target_at + max(WINDOW_TARGET - ta, 0)
    target_due = target_due and not held
    if soft <= 0:
        # GH #1272: before the abort of a window without a package.
        if day_due:
            return {"mark": "day", "rebuild_to": ta}
        if target_due:
            return {"mark": "target", "rebuild_to": ta}
        return dict({"mark": "none", "rebuild_to": rb}, **({"hold": int(target_at)} if held else {}))
    mark = "none"
    hard = lim.get("input_hard", 0)
    if hard > 0 and (window > hard or (next_estimate or 0) >= HARD_HEADROOM * hard):
        mark = "hard"
    elif window >= soft:
        mark = "soft"
    elif day_due:
        mark, rb = "day", ta or rb
    elif target_due:
        mark, rb = "target", ta
    elif lim.get("cost_in", 0) > 0 and lim.get("cost_cached_in", 0) > 0 \
            and not (lim.get("price_tiers")
                     and (held or (WINDOW_TARGET > 0 and window <= WINDOW_TARGET))):
        cb = cost_aim_of(lim)
        if cb > 0 and window > cb:
            due = amortise_after(window, cb, lim["cost_in"], lim["cost_cached_in"], lim)
            if due is not None and n >= due:
                mark, rb = "cost", cb
    return dict({"mark": mark, "rebuild_to": rb},
                **({"hold": int(target_at)} if held and mark == "none" else {}))


def cost_cents(window, cached, limits):
    """The estimate of a turn's input in cents: `turn_cost` (GH #1431), the
    one price of a turn the cost rule reads too."""
    return turn_cost(window, cached, limits)

def stamp_after(stamp, ms):

    a stamp that does not parse (the mark then goes at the next call)."""
    us = epoch_us(stamp)

            + datetime.timedelta(microseconds=us + ms * 1000)).strftime(FMT)
