LIVE_TURN_KEY = "live_turn:"


def live_of(seam_hop):
    """D58 live (GH #1482, contract point 1): the handle of the running
    session a turn belongs to -- `live` of the seam's hop, else of the context
    (the carrier across cells; the edges of a composition set it). "" = the
    turn belongs to no session of its own."""
    seam_hop = seam_hop if isinstance(seam_hop, dict) else {}
    return str(seam_hop.get("live") or ctx.get("live") or "")


# The facts of the last seed (`./history`) or feed (here) of a call -- one row
# per call, written by both, compared before a feed leaves.
SEED_FACTS_KEY = "seed_facts:"
# THE TOPIC'S AGE (GH #1436, review C2): the live feed reads the topic a seed
# of the call carries, and with `topic_aging` "1" `./history` ages it -- a feed
# reading it unaged parted the digests and fed the old topic back into the call
# on every closed turn. So the feed ages it by the same rule, the same switch,
# the same params (`topic_aged`, one text in both cells). "0" (the default) =
# the feed's reads and digests as before. `live_opened:<live>` is the running
# session's opening as `./history` wrote it with the opening seed (D58 live).
TOPIC_AGING = str(P.get("topic_aging") or "0").strip() == "1"
TOPIC_AGE_TURNS = max(1, _int("topic_age_turns", 4))
# The bound of the read that counts the turns since the naming (the person's
# rows, one per turn): a set's number (R-IG-1), above `topic_age_turns`.
TOPIC_AGE_ROWS = max(1, _int("topic_age_rows", 16))
LIVE_OPENED_KEY = "live_opened:"
# THE START WINDOW'S TARGET (D58 judge, GH #1480): the target whose family
# the live feed of a running session carries, as the seed does -- the
# contributions the domains leave for it, one state row each under
# `part_key` (`./history`, `part_row`). A set's name, the same knob and value
# as `./history`'s; "" (the default) = none.
SEED_TARGET = str(P.get("seed_target") or "").strip()
# The most contributions the feed reads of the family, per range (R-IG-1:
# the set's number, the same preset as `./history`'s).
PART_ROWS = max(1, _int("part_rows", 64))


# >>> parts (D58 judge, GH #1480): each function ONE text in every cell that holds it
# (`./history`, `./policy`, `./intake`; the lock `gh_d58_judge_parts_are_one_text`)
def part_key(target, subject, source):
    """The `state` key of one contribution: target, subject ("" for none) and
    source as one JSON list, so the family of a target (and a subject) is one
    key range and no name can run into another."""
    return "part:" + json.dumps([target, subject, source], ensure_ascii=False,
                                separators=(",", ":"))


def part_range(target, subject):
    """The first key of the family of `target` for `subject` ("" for none):
    every key of it starts so, and a range read stops at the first that does
    not."""
    return part_key(target, subject, "")[:-3]


def part_until_ms(until):
    """An `until` as epoch milliseconds, None when it is no RFC 3339 instant."""
    try:
        t = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(str(until).replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    except ValueError:
        return None
    if t.tzinfo is None:
        t = t.replace(tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
    return int(t.timestamp() * 1000)


def part_leaf(value):
    """A contribution as a leaf of the system tree: text as it came, anything
    else as its JSON text -- never read, never cut."""
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return {"text": value}
    return {"text": json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))}


def part_now_ms():
    """The instant an `until` is measured against: the param `now_utc` (RFC
    3339, the lab clock) when set, the clock otherwise."""
    fixed = part_until_ms(str(P.get("now_utc") or "").strip())
    return fixed if fixed is not None else now_ms()


def part_family(own, about, target, person, round_value, bound):
    """The family of `target` out of two range reads -- `own` the
    contributions without a subject, `about` those about the round's `person`
    -- as `{source: leaf}`, one leaf per source. A contribution about the
    person stands only for a round that is a subset of the one it came from
    (R-AF-3) and wins over one of the same source without a subject; an ended
    one (`until` passed) stands no more. A read that came back with `bound`
    rows is said on stderr."""
    family, now_at = {}, part_now_ms()
    for got, subject in ((own, ""), (about if person else [], person)):
        if len(got) >= bound:
            sys.stderr.write("curator: the family of %r holds %d contributions or more"
                             " (part_rows) -- the rest stays out\n" % (target, bound))
        first = part_range(target, subject)
        for r in got:
            if not str(r.get("key") or "").startswith(first):
                break
            try:
                held = json.loads(str(r.get("value") or ""))
            except ValueError:
                continue
            if not isinstance(held, dict) or "value" not in held:
                continue
            if subject and not allowed(round_value, held.get("round")):
                continue
            end = part_until_ms(held["until"]) if held.get("until") is not None else None
            if end is not None and end <= now_at:
                continue
            family[str(held.get("source") or "")] = part_leaf(held["value"])
    return family


def leaf_names(leaf):
    """What a contribution names, for the seed's fact line, the live facts and
    the live feed alike: the `name` of every entry of a structured list that
    carries one (by structure, never by a word); else the leaf's text as it
    came."""
    text = str((leaf or {}).get("text") or "") if isinstance(leaf, dict) else ""
    try:
        value = json.loads(text) if text else None
    except ValueError:
        value = None
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [str(x["name"]).strip() for x in value
                if isinstance(x, dict) and str(x.get("name") or "").strip()]
    return [text.strip()] if text.strip() else []


def family_names(family):
    """What a family names, `{source: [name, ...]}` in the order of the
    sources' names, a source that names nothing left out: one reading for the
    seed's fact line, the live facts and the live feed (review I3 of the D58
    judge strand: the feed and the live facts carried the whole contribution,
    the fact line its names; before the strand the feed carried the screen
    topics' names alone)."""
    out = {}
    for source in sorted(family or {}):
        names = leaf_names(family[source])
        if names:
            out[source] = names
    return out


def parts_text(family):
    """A family as one canonical text: what the facts digest of a seed and of
    the live feed compares ("" for none)."""
    if not family:
        return ""
    return json.dumps(family, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
# <<< parts


def live_parts(lg_):
    """The family of the start window's target the feed read (`l-part`), as
    the seed reads it: the contributions without a subject ({} for no target;
    OR-d58-2.judge.12 -- a seed never carried a person's hints, so its digest
    and the feed's leave them out alike)."""
    if not SEED_TARGET:
        return {}
    return part_family(rows(lg_, "l-part"), [], SEED_TARGET, "", the_round, PART_ROWS)
MOVES = ("start", "continue", "end")
NOTHING_TOPIC = json.dumps({"movement": "continue", "name": ""}, sort_keys=True,
                           separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)
INNER_KINDS = ["advice", "delegation", "event"]
INNER_READ = 20
# What the end of a text may lose before two texts are compared (the same
# cut as `talky/route`'s `normalize`).
TRAILING = ".!?…,;: \t\r\n"
TOOL_ERROR_NOTE = ("tool not reachable: a tool this turn called gave no usable result; "
                   "what it returned is not shown to the person.")


def normalize(text):
    """The text as it is compared: one space between words, lower case, no trailing
    punctuation or space."""
    return " ".join(str(text or "").split()).lower().rstrip(TRAILING)


def heard_text(wall, session, turn):
    """The person's words of a turn on the wall, in order."""
    out = []
    for r in sorted([r for r in wall or [] if isinstance(r, dict)
                     and str(r.get("session_id") or "") == session
                     and str(r.get("turn_id") or "") == turn
                     and str(r.get("kind") or "") == "user"],
                    key=lambda r: int(r.get("seq") or 0)):
        el = element_of(r) or {}
        if el.get("type") == "text" and str(el.get("text") or "").strip():
            out.append(str(el.get("text")))
    return " ".join(out)


def delta_hop(seam, stamp_):
    """The seam of a spec curate as the normal curate of the delta's stamp:
    no `spec`, the delta's path, needs, families and turn notes."""
    h = {k: v for k, v in seam.items() if k != "spec"}
    h["path"] = str(stamp_.get("path") or "")
    h["needs"] = ",".join(names_list(stamp_.get("needs")))
    h["families"] = ",".join(names_list(stamp_.get("families")))
    notes = [n for n in stamp_.get("turn_notes") or [] if isinstance(n, dict)
             and str(n.get("text") or "").strip()]
    h["turn_notes"] = json.dumps(notes, ensure_ascii=False) if notes else ""
    # D54g (GH #1506): the delta's move with its path -- a spec seam carries no
    # stamp key of its own. Only when the stamp names one: without, the hop is
    # the hop of before.
    h.pop("move", None)
    if str(stamp_.get("move") or "").strip():
        h["move"] = str(stamp_.get("move")).strip()
    return h


def delta_mark(cid, session, turn, call_, verdict, stamp_, why=""):
    value = {"turn_id": turn, "verdict": verdict, "call": call_}
    if why:
        value["reason"] = why
    return (cid, ins("marks", with_audience({
        "seq": epoch_us(stamp_) + 8, "session_id": session, "turn_id": turn,
        "kind": "delta", "value": canonical(value), "at": stamp_}, the_round)))


def unsent_ops(prefix, ids):
    """The records of calls built but never sent: `calls`, `call_blocks`,
    the -esc copy and the projection."""
    ids = [c for c in ids if c]
    if not ids:
        return []
    return [(prefix + "call", {"operation": "delete", "table": "calls",
                               "where": {"call_id": {"in": ids}}}),
            (prefix + "blk", {"operation": "delete", "table": "call_blocks",
                              "where": {"call_id": {"in": ids}}}),
            (prefix + "esc", {"operation": "delete", "table": "state",
                              "where": {"key": {"in": ["pending:" + c + ESC_SUFFIX for c in ids]
                                                + ["window_est:" + c for c in ids]}}})]


def sends_calls(sends):
    return [str((m.get("header") or {}).get("curator_call") or "")
            for m in sends or [] if isinstance(m, dict)]


def live_reads(session, turn):
    """The first read of a closed turn's live feed: its turn row (which
    names the handle). The facts are read in phase `live-facts`, once the
    handle -- the key of the last seed's facts -- is known."""
    return [("l-st", sel("state", ["key", "value"], {"key": {"in": [
               LIVE_TURN_KEY + "%s#%s" % (session, turn)]}}))]


def live_fact_reads(session, live):
    """The reads of the facts a seed of the handle `live` carries
    (`./history` reads them the same way for the seed): the facts of the last
    seed or feed of the handle, the notes, the newest inner turns and the newest named topic of the
    round, the contributions to the start window's target."""
    # D54g kprofil (#1507): the limits the handle's target named with its ask
    # for a start window (`seed_limits:<live>`, written by `./history`), in
    # the read that is made anyway. No row: everything as before.
    st_keys = [SEED_FACTS_KEY + live, SEED_LIMITS_KEY + live]
    topic_cols = ["seq", "session_id", "value", "audience_set"]
    if TOPIC_AGING:
        # GH #1436: the topic aged as the seed ages it -- the session's opening,
        # the naming mark's turn and (below) the person's rows that count the
        # turns. Off, the reads as before.
        st_keys.append(LIVE_OPENED_KEY + live)
        topic_cols = ["seq", "session_id", "turn_id", "value", "audience_set"]
    ops = [("l-st", sel("state", ["key", "value"], {"key": {"in": st_keys}})),
           ("l-notes", round_sel("notes", NOTE_READ_COLS, None, the_round, None)),
           ("l-inner", round_sel("wall", ["seq", "session_id", "turn_id", "kind", "hash",
                                          "audience_set"],
                                 {"kind": {"in": INNER_KINDS}},
                                 the_round, session, [("seq", "desc")], INNER_READ)),
           ("l-topic", round_sel("marks", topic_cols,
                                 {"kind": "topic", "value": {"neq": NOTHING_TOPIC}},
                                 the_round, session, [("seq", "desc")], 1))]
    if SEED_TARGET:
        # D58 judge (GH #1480): the family of the start window's target, the
        # contributions without a subject, one key range -- the read of
        # `./history`'s `part_reads(SEED_TARGET, "")` (OR-d58-2.judge.12).
        ops.append(("l-part", sel("state", ["key", "value"],
                                  {"key": {"gte": part_range(SEED_TARGET, "")}},
                                  [("key", "asc")], PART_ROWS)))
    if TOPIC_AGING:
        ops.append(("l-age", round_sel("wall", ["seq", "session_id", "turn_id", "audience_set"],
                                       {"kind": "user"}, the_round, session,
                                       [("seq", "desc")], TOPIC_AGE_ROWS)))
    return [(cid, a) for cid, a in ops if a is not None]


def live_change(lg_, session, last, live=""):
    """`(state, change)`: the facts a seed of the handle carries as they stand
    now (`seed_fact_state`) and what of them is new against `last` (the
    state of the handle's last seed or feed, {} for none) -- one source with
    the seed: what is fed is what the next seed says."""
    st = state_of(lg_, "l-st")
    l_notes = [r for r in rows(lg_, "l-notes") if allowed(the_round, r.get("audience_set"))]
    # Review o15-Rv1 m2: the seed's notes, one per item with the knob.
    notes = seed_notes(rows_latest_per_item(l_notes) if NOTES_PER_ITEM else l_notes, now_ms(),
                       live)
    inner = [r for r in rows(lg_, "l-inner") if passes(r, the_round, session)]
    inner_seq = max([int(r.get("seq") or 0) for r in inner] or [0])
    named = [r for r in rows(lg_, "l-topic") if passes(r, the_round, session)]
    topic = topic_now(named)
    if TOPIC_AGING and "l-age" in lg_:
        # GH #1436: aged as the seed ages it (`topic_aged`); the closed turn's
        # session asks, the session's opening as the opening seed wrote it.
        aged = rows(lg_, "l-age")
        topic = topic_aged(topic, named[0] if named else None,
                           [r for r in aged if passes(r, the_round, session)], session,
                           live_opened_of(st.get(LIVE_OPENED_KEY + live, "")),
                           len(aged) >= TOPIC_AGE_ROWS)
    family = live_parts(lg_)
    state = seed_fact_state(notes, inner_seq, topic, parts_text(family))
    if last.get("digest") == state["digest"]:
        return state, {}
    change = {}
    seen = set(last.get("notes") or [])
    new_notes = [{"source": n["source"], "id": n["id"], "text": n["text"]} for n in notes
                 if "%s:%s" % (n["source"], n["id"]) not in seen]
    if new_notes:
        change["notes"] = new_notes
    since = int(last.get("inner_seq") or 0)
    new_inner = [{"turn_id": str(r.get("turn_id") or ""), "kind": str(r.get("kind") or "")}
                 for r in sorted(inner, key=lambda r: int(r.get("seq") or 0))
                 if int(r.get("seq") or 0) > since]
    if new_inner:
        change["inner_turns"] = new_inner
    if topic != str(last.get("topic") or ""):
        change["topic"] = topic
    if state["parts"] != str(last.get("parts") or ""):
        # D58 judge: what the family names as it stands now, per source, as the
        # seed's fact line names it (`family_names`; review I3, OR-d58-2.judge.16)
        # -- the names, never the whole contribution.
        change["parts"] = family_names(family)
    if not change:
        # The digest moved by what no field says (a note gone, an inner turn
        # dropped out of the gate): the seed differs, the feed says so.
        change["notes"] = []
    return state, change


# >>> own-feed-by-target v1 (D54g kprofil, #1507, contract point 4)
# THE OWN FEED FOLLOWS THE TARGET. With `live_feed` on, every move of the
# start window's facts after a closed turn sent a wordless `renew`: a new
# session, a new start window -- also for a topic the person raised in that
# very session (measured: four renewals in eight sessions, three of them into
# running speech). A target that holds its own session names its limits in
# its ask for a start window; `./history` holds them per handle
# (`seed_limits:<live>`, the canonical JSON of `limits`), and the field
# `feed_own` of their `profile` says what the own feed does:
#
#   renew    (shipped, and every handle without the row or the field) as
#            before: `live_change`, one wordless feed, section `renew`.
#   context  ONE feed, section `context`, with words under `payload`: only
#            what came from OUTSIDE since the handle's last start window or
#            feed -- a new note, a new inner turn (memory arrives as one of
#            the two). The topic and the contributions to the start window's
#            target move nothing here (OR-d54g.kprofil.6: a contribution
#            carries no mark of where it came from). An inner turn that has
#            a road of its own into the session moves nothing either
#            (`INNER_OWN_ROAD`, below). Whole units, the newest
#            first, greedy up to `feed_budget` tokens at the target's
#            `chars_per_token`; each unit begins with its place as the start
#            window writes it (`Notes: `, `(<kind>) `), because the target
#            sees it without the window around it, and an empty line parts
#            two units, so a unit of several lines stays one. A unit that
#            does not fit beside the others waits: the held state names only
#            what went, so the next closed turn takes it up. No unit is cut.
#            A unit over the budget ALONE goes alone and whole in the turn
#            whose feed would be empty without it (OR-d54g.kprofil.10): under
#            `context` no renewal comes from the session's own turns, so it
#            would never arrive; at most one such unit a turn, and the
#            receiver parts it.
#   none     no own feed.
#
# An ordered feed (`in_feed`), the tool fact and every other feed are not
# read here. `limits.model` is held, never read.
SEED_LIMITS_KEY = "seed_limits:"
FEED_OWN = ("renew", "context", "none")
# The place a note stands at in a start window (`./history`: one `Notes: `
# line), the inner turns the held state names as fed while an older one waits.
NOTE_PLACE = "Notes: "
INNER_FED = "inner_fed"
# What parts two units of one feed: an empty line. A note or an inner turn
# may run over several lines; joined by a single line break its later lines
# stood there without a place, like units of their own.
UNIT_SEP = "\n\n"
# The inner turns that are no news from outside under `context`
# (OR-d54g.kprofil.11 and .15: nothing reaches a session twice). A row of
# kind `delegation` is the errand the agent that holds the session handed
# out itself (`./intake` `kinds_of`: its own words, framed) -- a move of the
# session's own turns; its result comes back as the feed `fact`. A row of
# kind `advice` stands on the wall because the window of a model call of
# that round carried it (`./intake` files it from the request it curated),
# and the answer of that call takes its own road to the session. What is
# left is the kind `event`: a round nobody in the session spoke.
INNER_OWN_ROAD = ("delegation", "advice")


def seed_limits_of(st, live):
    """The limits the target of the handle `live` named with its ask for a
    start window, as `./history` holds them; {} for none (as before)."""
    raw = st.get(SEED_LIMITS_KEY + live, "")
    return loads(raw, {}) if raw else {}


def feed_own_of(limits):
    """What the own feed does for a target with these limits: the field
    `feed_own` of their profile, else the shipped value; a word that is none
    of `FEED_OWN` is said on stderr and read as the shipped one."""
    profile = limits.get("profile")
    v = profile.get("feed_own") if isinstance(profile, dict) else None
    if unset(v):
        return PROFILE_SHIPPED["feed_own"]
    v = str(v).strip().lower()
    if v not in FEED_OWN:
        sys.stderr.write("curator/policy: feed_own %r is none of %s -- %s\n"
                         % (v, "|".join(FEED_OWN), PROFILE_SHIPPED["feed_own"]))
        return PROFILE_SHIPPED["feed_own"]
    return v


def feed_room(limits):
    """`(room, in_chars)`: what one feed to a target with these limits may
    measure -- `feed_budget` tokens at its `chars_per_token`, counted in
    characters as the target counts and as `./history` cuts its start window
    (one rule in the hive); a target that names no rate is counted by this
    script's own estimate, UTF-8 bytes at `CHARS_PER_TOKEN`. `room` None: the
    target named no budget, so there is none to cut by (R-IG-1: the number
    is the asker's, never one of this code). A budget of 0 is named: room 0,
    the smallest feed -- one unit a turn (`live_packed`)."""
    def num(v, least=None):
        # The rule `./history` reads the same row by (`limit_number`): a
        # number, no bool, no text; above 0, a budget from 0 on.
        if isinstance(v, bool) or not isinstance(v, (int, float)) or v != v:
            return None
        if v < 0 or (v == 0 and least != 0):
            return None
        return v
    budget, rate = num(limits.get("feed_budget"), 0), num(limits.get("chars_per_token"))
    if budget is None:
        return None, rate is not None
    if rate is None:
        return int(budget * CHARS_PER_TOKEN), False
    # In thousandths of a character, whole numbers, as the target counts its
    # tokens: a text is inside the budget here exactly when the target's own
    # estimate of it is.
    milli = max(1, int(rate * 1000 + 0.5))
    return int(budget * milli // 1000), True


def live_outside(lg_, session, last, live=""):
    """`(units, note_keys, inner_seq)`: what came from outside since `last`
    (the state of the handle's last start window or feed), the newest first
    -- the notes a start window carries that `last` does not name, the inner
    turns behind its `inner_seq` it has not fed and that have no road of
    their own (`INNER_OWN_ROAD`) --, beside the keys of the
    notes as they stand now and the newest inner turn. The same reads and
    the same gate as `live_change`; the topic and the contributions are not
    looked at. `live`: the handle of the running session the feed is for."""
    l_notes = [r for r in rows(lg_, "l-notes") if allowed(the_round, r.get("audience_set"))]
    # GH #1436 (d58rest): the notes as `live_change` judges them, by the
    # handle -- a carried note born in this running session is no unit of
    # its own feed (`seed_notes`, `not_live`).
    notes = seed_notes(rows_latest_per_item(l_notes) if NOTES_PER_ITEM else l_notes, now_ms(),
                       live)
    keys = ["%s:%s" % (n["source"], n["id"]) for n in notes]
    seen = set(str(k) for k in last.get("notes") or [])
    units = [{"k": "note", "key": k, "at": epoch_us(n["at"]) or 0, "text": n["text"]}
             for k, n in zip(keys, notes) if k not in seen]
    inner = [r for r in rows(lg_, "l-inner") if passes(r, the_round, session)]
    since = int(last.get("inner_seq") or 0)
    fed = set(int(s) for s in last.get(INNER_FED) or [])
    for r in inner:
        seq = int(r.get("seq") or 0)
        if str(r.get("kind") or "") in INNER_OWN_ROAD:
            # Counted for the mark below, never a unit: it has its own road.
            continue
        if seq > since and seq not in fed:
            units.append({"k": "inner", "key": seq, "at": seq,
                          "kind": str(r.get("kind") or ""), "hash": str(r.get("hash") or "")})
    units.sort(key=lambda u: (u["at"], str(u["key"])), reverse=True)
    return units, keys, max([int(r.get("seq") or 0) for r in inner] or [0])


def live_packed(units, bodies, room, in_chars=False):
    """`(lines, taken)`: the units of `units` (newest first) that go into one
    feed of at most `room` characters, or UTF-8 bytes without `in_chars`
    (`feed_room`; None: no bound) -- whole units,
    greedy, each beginning with its place, `UNIT_SEP` between two --, and
    every unit that is done with: the ones in `lines` and an inner turn
    without words (its block is gone or empty; there is nothing to wait
    for). A unit that does not fit beside the ones before it is left out and
    waits. One that would not fit alone is never cut: it waits while
    anything else goes, and the newest such goes alone and whole when the
    feed would be empty without it (OR-d54g.kprofil.10), named on stderr."""
    lines, taken, used, over = [], [], 0, None
    for u in units:
        if u["k"] == "note":
            line = NOTE_PLACE + str(u.get("text") or "")
        else:
            el = element_of({"body": bodies.get(str(u.get("hash") or ""))})
            text = stripped_text(str((el or {}).get("text") or ""))
            if not text.strip():
                taken.append(u)
                continue
            line = "(%s) %s" % (u.get("kind") or "", text)
        size = len(line) if in_chars else len(line.encode("utf-8"))
        if room is not None and size > room:
            if over is None:
                over = (u, line, size)
            continue
        sep = len(UNIT_SEP) if lines else 0
        if room is not None and used + size + sep > room:
            continue
        used += size + sep
        lines.append(line)
        taken.append(u)
    if over is not None and not lines:
        u, line, size = over
        sys.stderr.write("curator/policy: a unit of the own feed (%s %s, size %d) is over"
                         " the feed budget of its target (%d) -- not cut, it goes alone"
                         " and whole\n" % (u["k"], u["key"], size, room))
        lines.append(line)
        taken.append(u)
    return lines, taken


def live_fed_state(last, units, taken, note_keys, inner_seq):
    """The held state of the handle after a feed of `taken` out of `units`:
    the notes as they stand now without the ones that wait; the inner mark
    moved up to the newest turn once none waits, else left where it is with
    the fed ones named beside it (`inner_fed`); the topic and the
    contributions as `last` has them -- they were not fed. Digest by the rule
    of `seed_fact_state` (the state without its digest, keys sorted)."""
    done = set((u["k"], str(u["key"])) for u in taken)
    waiting = [u for u in units if (u["k"], str(u["key"])) not in done]
    wait_notes = set(u["key"] for u in waiting if u["k"] == "note")
    since = int(last.get("inner_seq") or 0)
    out = dict((k, v) for k, v in last.items() if k not in ("digest", INNER_FED))
    out["notes"] = sorted(k for k in note_keys if k not in wait_notes)
    out["topic"] = str(last.get("topic") or "")
    out["parts"] = str(last.get("parts") or "")
    if any(u["k"] == "inner" for u in waiting):
        out["inner_seq"] = since
        out[INNER_FED] = sorted(set([int(s) for s in last.get(INNER_FED) or [] if int(s) > since]
                                    + [int(u["key"]) for u in taken if u["k"] == "inner"]))
    else:
        out["inner_seq"] = max(since, int(inner_seq or 0))
    out["digest"] = hashlib.sha256(
        json.dumps(out, sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]
    return out


def live_context_out(plan, bodies):
    """The step that ends a closed turn's own feed for a target with
    `feed_own` `context`: the messages to emit ([] for nothing). `plan` is
    what phase `live-facts` found (`s`, `t`, `c`: session, turn, handle; `u`
    the units, `n` the note keys, `i` the newest inner turn, `w` the held
    state as read, `r` the room of one feed as `feed_room` gives it), `bodies` the blocks of the
    inner turns among the units. The held state is set by compare-and-set
    on the value read when there was one (`./history` writes the key with
    every start window; lost, its state stands and is true), and the feed
    takes the one road of every own feed (`own_feed`, `feed_out`): its mark
    `feed` rides the same step and says how many units went and how many
    wait."""
    units = [u for u in plan.get("u") or [] if isinstance(u, dict)]
    live, raw = str(plan.get("c") or ""), str(plan.get("w") or "")
    last = loads(raw, {}) if raw else {}
    room = plan.get("r") if isinstance(plan.get("r"), list) and len(plan.get("r")) == 2 \
        else [None, False]
    lines, taken = live_packed(units, bodies, room[0], bool(room[1]))
    if not taken:
        return []
    value = canonical(live_fed_state(last, units, taken, plan.get("n") or [], plan.get("i")))
    key = SEED_FACTS_KEY + live
    ops = [("l-sent", upd("state", {"value": value}, {"key": key, "value": raw}))] if raw \
        else put("l-sent", key, value)
    l_msg = None
    if lines:
        head = {"section": "context", "live": live, "session_id": str(plan.get("s") or ""),
                "turn_id": str(plan.get("t") or "")}
        l_ops, l_msg = feed_out(own_feed(head, {"payload": UNIT_SEP.join(lines), "messages": []},
                                         the_round,
                                         mark={"units": len(lines),
                                               "waiting": len(units) - len(taken)}))
        ops += l_ops

def topic_of(value):
    """(movement, name) of one `topic` mark in the form OR-KY-71 writes --
    canonical JSON `{"movement": .., "name": ..}`, `name` empty when the memory
    section named none -- or None for any other value."""
    try:
        v = json.loads(str(value or ""))
    except Exception:
        return None
    if not isinstance(v, dict):
        return None
    movement = str(v.get("movement") or "").strip().lower()
    if movement not in MOVES:

    ended the topic or there is none."""
    for m in marks:
        t = topic_of(m.get("value"))
        if t is not None:
            return "" if t[0] == "end" else t[1]

def rows_latest_per_item(note_rows):
    """D38 V1 (review o15-Rv1 m2): the `notes` rows without the older of one
    `(source, item)` -- the youngest by `at`, then `note_id`, stands (the
    window's `latest_per_item`); a row without an item always stays. ONE
    text in `./history` (the seed) and `./policy` (the feed), behind the
    one knob `notes_latest_per_item`."""
    best = {}
    for r in note_rows:
        item = str(r.get("item") or "")
        if item:
            k = (str(r.get("source") or ""), item)
            rank = (str(r.get("at") or ""), str(r.get("note_id") or ""))
            if k not in best or rank > best[k][0]:
                best[k] = (rank, r)
    return [r for r in note_rows if not str(r.get("item") or "")
            or best[(str(r.get("source") or ""), str(r.get("item") or ""))][1] is r]


def topic_aged(topic, named, wall, session_now="", opened_seq=0, full=False):
    """GH #1436: `topic` as it frames the asking turn now. ONE rule in two
    cells, this text byte for byte in `./history` (the route stamp, the judge,
    the seed of a call) and `./policy` (the live feed of a call) -- two
    readers of one fact parted once (the feed fed back what the seed had aged
    out), `gh1436_d` holds the twins equal. `named` is the mark that last
    named the topic (`{seq, session_id, turn_id?}`), `wall` the person's rows
    of the read's scope (`kind` `user`, one per turn, newest first, through
    the gate, the running turn left out), `session_now` the asking session
    ("" = the session of the newest row of `wall`), `opened_seq` the seq the
    asking call opened at (0 = unknown), `full` the `wall` read came back
    with `topic_age_rows` rows. "" when the call opened after the naming,
    when the asking session is not the naming one, or once `topic_age_turns`
    turns stood after the naming -- turns, not marks: a tool round or an
    answer without its `memory` block leaves no mark and is a turn all the
    same. A full read that never reached the naming counts as the bound.
    Off (`topic_aging` "0"): `topic` as read."""
    if not TOPIC_AGING or not topic or named is None:
        return topic
    seq = int(named.get("seq") or 0)
    if opened_seq and seq < int(opened_seq):
        return ""
    sess = str(session_now or "") or (str(wall[0].get("session_id") or "") if wall else "")
    if sess and sess != str(named.get("session_id") or ""):
        return ""
    later = {(str(r.get("session_id") or ""), str(r.get("turn_id") or ""))
             for r in wall if int(r.get("seq") or 0) > seq}
    if named.get("turn_id"):
        later.discard((str(named.get("session_id") or ""), str(named.get("turn_id") or "")))
    if len(later) >= TOPIC_AGE_TURNS:
        return ""
    if full and not any(int(r.get("seq") or 0) <= seq for r in wall):
        return ""
    return topic

def seed_notes(note_rows, stamp_ms, live):
    """GH #1279: the notes a seed carries and a live feed watches -- the
    session and until notes among `note_rows` (already through the round's
    gate) with a text and an `until` not passed, oldest first; a turn note
    is its own turn's and never a fact of the call. The same text in
    `./history` (the seed) and `./policy` (the feed), pinned. `live`: the
    handle of the running session the seed or feed is for."""
    out = []
    for r in note_rows:
        text = str(r.get("text") or "")
        if not text.strip() or str(r.get("scope") or "") not in ("session", "until"):
            continue
        u = epoch_ms(r.get("until"))
        if str(r.get("until") or "").strip() and u is not None and u <= stamp_ms:
            continue
        # GH #1436: a carried note is no fact of the running session it was
        # born in (`not_live`, `carried_notes`): neither its seed nor its
        # feed. A seed names the session by its handle, the turns by the
        # session of their generation -- the handle is the one id both share.
        if str(r.get("not_live") or "") and str(r.get("not_live")) == str(live or ""):
            continue
        out.append({"source": str(r.get("source") or ""), "id": str(r.get("note_id") or ""),
                    "text": text, "at": str(r.get("at") or "")})
    return sorted(out, key=lambda n: (n["at"], n["source"], n["id"]))


def seed_fact_state(notes, inner_seq, topic, parts_raw):
    """GH #1279: the facts of a seed as one comparable state -- the note
    ids, the newest inner turn, the topic and the contributions to the start
    window's target as one text (`parts_text`, D58 judge) -- and their digest. `./history` keeps the state of the seed it sent,
    `./policy` the state of the feed it sent, under the same key
    (`seed_facts:<call>`); a feed leaves only when the digest moved."""
    state = {"notes": sorted("%s:%s" % (n["source"], n["id"]) for n in notes),
             "inner_seq": int(inner_seq or 0), "topic": str(topic or ""),
             "parts": hashlib.sha256(str(parts_raw or "").encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]}
    state["digest"] = hashlib.sha256(
        json.dumps(state, sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]
    return state

def open_tools(scope, places):
    """The tools the cut left open for a call, as a side text names them: the
    scope's `allow` without its hint-stage families (named, not callable). A
    family with a row in `places` stands once by its family name
    (`web_search`, `web_fetch` -> `web`); the stamp is no guide here -- the
    lab stamped its weather turns `web` (r026e, all eleven tool rounds)."""
    scope = scope if isinstance(scope, dict) else {}
    hint = names_list(scope.get("hint"))
    out = []
    for name in names_list(scope.get("allow")):
        if name in hint:
            continue
        fam = name.split("_")[0]
        key = fam if fam in places else name
        if key not in out:

def places_phrase(tools, places, rest, join):
    """The open tools in the words of `places`, joined by `join`. Words, never
    a tool's code name (GH #1260, BL6 arms A and B: told the code name, the
    fast model wrote the call out or spoke made-up results in 14 of 30 probe
    sentences, the words held 0 of 30). A tool without a row is not named:
    beside named ones it adds `rest`, alone it leaves the place out."""
    named = [places[n] for n in tools if n in places]
    if named and len(named) < len(tools) and rest:
        named.append(rest)
    return join.join(named)


def side_fill(text, fill, scope):
    """The side text with its gap (`SIDE_GAP`) filled from `fill` over the
    tools the cut left open (`scope`, the call's `tool_scope`): `before` and
    the phrase, or nothing when no tool is named. A text without the gap
    stays as it is."""
    if SIDE_GAP not in text:
        return text
    fill = fill if isinstance(fill, dict) else {}
    places = fill.get("places") if isinstance(fill.get("places"), dict) else {}
    places = dict((str(k), v) for k, v in places.items() if isinstance(v, str) and v)
    phrase = places_phrase(open_tools(scope, places), places, str(fill.get("rest") or ""),
                           str(fill.get("join") or " "))
    return text.replace(SIDE_GAP, (str(fill.get("before") or "") + phrase) if phrase else "")


def turn_window(msgs):
    """The person's own turn out of a window, nothing before it -- the
    window `turn` of a side entry and of a profile. GH #1260 fix round 1
    (OR-WG-13): an earlier answer in the window is a pattern the fast model
    follows -- it answered the consult in the sentence itself (a plan, a
    table, pros and cons) in 3 of 5 probe sentences as logged and 5 of 12
    with a sharper instruction, and asked "how cold tonight in Berlin?"
    after two short answers it said the degrees in 7 of 20 (17 of 20 with
    that wording); with the person's turn alone 0 of 12 and 0 of 20, all tool
    rounds 0 of 30 (BL6 arm C2). No text of the person in the window (an
    empty window, only pins, only answers): the window without its pins
    (delta review 2 of U, M1) -- a pin is never the only `{origin: user}`
    element of a side call.

    The turn is every text of the person since the last message that is not
    theirs, in order: a request sent in two messages ("how cold tonight?" /
    "in Berlin") keeps both (fix-round review M1). A pin is never part of it
    (`is_pin`): with `broadcast_mode` tail it stands as `{origin: user}`
    where it arrived, behind the turn when it came after it, and taken for
    the turn it made the side call lose the request (fix-round review I1)."""
    turn = []
    for el in reversed(msgs):
        if is_pin(el):
            continue
        if isinstance(el, dict) and el.get("type") == "text" and \
                el.get("origin") in ("user", "peer"):
            turn.append(el)
        elif turn:
            break
    if turn:
        return list(reversed(turn))
    return [el for el in msgs if not is_pin(el)]

    person's turn alone (`turn_window`), `wall` the target's window."""

def is_pin(el):
    """A pin standing as a message (`pin_split`'s tail): its text in
    `PIN_FRAME`, behind the short id the window may put first."""
    if not isinstance(el, dict) or el.get("type") != "text":
        return False
    text = str(el.get("text") or "")
    if text.startswith("[#") and "] " in text:
        text = text[text.index("] ") + 2:]
    return text.startswith(PIN_FRAME.split("%s")[0])

# byte (a lock holds the two): a contract this hive cuts gets its frame anew

SIDECAR_PREAMBLE = (
    "After your answer -- always after, never instead of it -- append ONE "
    "fenced block that opens with ```sidecar, holds ONE JSON object and nothing "
    "else, and closes with ```. One top-level key per section, all inside the "
    "one outer object:")


def frame_slot(skeleton):
    """The FORM one section's body takes in the shape line (GH #799): `{...}`
    for an object, `[...]` for a list, `"..."` for a string, the literal for
    a number, a boolean or null -- the brackets a model has to write, never a
    second copy of the example."""
    if isinstance(skeleton, dict):
        return "{...}"
    if isinstance(skeleton, list):
        return "[...]"
    if isinstance(skeleton, str):
        return "\"...\""
    return json.dumps(skeleton, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)


def sidecar_frame(req, opt):
    """The frame of the block contract over the sections it holds (GH #606):
    the preamble, the whole-object shape, the obligation by name. `req` and
    `opt` are `(name, slot)` pairs, required and optional, in the order the
    sections stand. `collector/assemble` writes it over every offered
    section; `curator/policy` writes it anew over the sections it kept, so
    the frame never asks for a section the contract left out (GH #1085)."""
    def names(items):
        return ", ".join('"%s"' % n for n, _ in items)
    shape = "{" + ", ".join('"%s": %s' % (n, s) for n, s in req + opt) + "}"
    parts = [SIDECAR_PREAMBLE, shape]
    if req:
        line = ("%s %s written on EVERY turn, even the ones that changed nothing"
                % (names(req), "is" if len(req) == 1 else "are"))
        line += (", and when %s %s present too: an optional section never"
                 " replaces a required one."
                 % (names(opt), "is" if len(opt) == 1 else "are")
                 if opt else "; leaving one out is a fault.")
        parts.append(line)
    if opt:
        parts.append("Write %s only when it applies; otherwise leave its key"
                     " out." % names(opt))
    return "\n".join(parts)

DAY_MS = 86400000

MODEL_SOURCE = "model"

GATED_FAMILIES = ("history", "pinned")

SESSION_SLOTS = tuple(p for p in ("roster", ERRAND_SLOT, "instructions.mode",

# THE SYSTEM OF ONE TURN (GH #1298). A brain answers a turn in several calls
# -- one per tool round -- and a provider that signs its thinking binds every
# block to the system it was made under: the Messages wire refuses the replay
# of a tool round's thinking once `system` differs (400 "Invalid signature in
# thinking block ... The system prompt differs"). Measured in production
# (talky, native Anthropic brain): the quick voice's answers had left its
# window in state (`input_soft` 20000), the brain's first call cut the sidecar
# contract to it, the brain's own answer stamped 90000, the call after the
# tool result carried the whole contract -- `instructions` changed, the turn
# died after its interim sentence. So the leaves of the first brain call of a
# turn are kept (`turn_system:<session>:<turn>`, the turn, its round) and
# every later brain call of the same turn and round sends exactly them:
# what changes between the rounds of a turn (a slot, a pin, a consult's
# mark) reaches the model with the next turn, never inside one.
# Review M1 of F2: the cause itself is gone as well -- the tap keeps the
# window (`input_soft`/`input_hard`) of an answer under its target
# (`catalog:<target>:<key>`, D58 target), and the wall's under the bare keys
# only from a target that holds its tree, so a quick answer no longer cuts
# the brain's contract, renders its earlier answers or guards its hard line. The row also holds the window the leaves were
# fitted to (`soft`, `hard`) and the contract cuts said with them: every
# call of the turn renders the earlier answers' sidecar blocks alike (the
# `messages` prefix before a replayed thinking block stays) and says the
# cuts it sends (review m1). One row per turn (review m3): two turns of a
# session never overwrite each other's; the tap takes it down when the
# brain's answer ends the turn; a row a round left (a hand-over, a lost
# answer) goes with the first call of a later turn of the session once it is
# older than `pending_sweep_s` (the session's list `turn_system_last:<session>`)
# -- the store holds the rows of the turns that run, never one per turn.
# Not frozen: `tools` (review m2). A consult the brain starts in a round
# is refused to every later call of the session while it runs (GH #1280) --
# since GH #1497 at the call (`hop.tools_refused`, the dispatcher), no more
# by a deny in `tools`, so the menu stays -- and its `consult.pending` note
# joins the notes block with the next turn (GH #1497: the tail, never the
# system part): within the turn the brain has its own call and its result.
TURN_SYSTEM = "turn_system:"
TURN_SYSTEM_LAST = "turn_system_last:"


def turn_system_key(session, turn):
    """The state key of the system row of one turn (review m3 of F2)."""
    return TURN_SYSTEM + session + ":" + turn


def turn_system_of(raw, turn, the_round, target):
    """The row of the first brain call of `turn` in `the_round`, kept in the
    state row `raw` (GH #1298): `{"leaves": [(path, text, hash)], "soft",
    "hard", "cuts", "target"}`; None when the row is another turn's, another
    round's, another target's (GH #1512), carries no target or is unreadable
    -- the call then builds its own and keeps it."""
    kept = loads(raw, {})
    if not turn or kept.get("turn") != turn or kept.get("round") != round_canon(the_round):
        return None
    # GH #1512: the row is bound to the target whose call wrote it. Measured
    # in the lab (twice): a row another target's call of the turn wrote held
    # THAT call's notes block, and the speaker took it frozen -- the turn's
    # crisis note (`route.risk`, priority 0) never reached it. A row without
    # a target is no one's: the call builds its own (the safe direction).
    if "target" not in kept or kept.get("target") != target:
        return None
    leaves = kept.get("leaves")
    if not isinstance(leaves, list):
        return None
    out = []
    for x in leaves:
        if not (isinstance(x, list) and len(x) == 3 and all(isinstance(v, str) for v in x)):
            return None
        out.append(tuple(x))
    cuts = kept.get("cuts")
    notes = kept.get("notes")
    return {"leaves": out, "soft": str(kept.get("soft") or ""),
            "hard": str(kept.get("hard") or ""),
            "cuts": [c for c in cuts if isinstance(c, dict)] if isinstance(cuts, list) else [],
            "notes": notes if isinstance(notes, dict) else None}
# THE IDENTITY BUDGET (GH #935, OR-S3-71). An identity pusher may hold a
# short form of the identity beside the whole one (`identity_short`). With
# `split` the system part carries ONLY the short form, as the `identity`
# family, in every call; the whole pack is ONE element of the window
# (`messages[0]`), a SNAPSHOT block of its own kind, taken at call 1, after a
# rebuild and after a renewal of the call's own session, and sent byte for
# byte the same until the next of these -- a later call takes no new
# snapshot, and the block is never trimmed. Why: the system part is re-sent
# on every change, a message at the head of the window is part of the cached
# prefix and costs once per snapshot.
IDENTITY_FAMILY = "identity"
SHORT_FAMILY = "identity_short"
IDENTITY_FULL_KIND = "identity_full"
# What decides whether a snapshot still holds: the session, the epoch of the
# window as the session sees it (`window_epoch`), the last renewal of the
# session (state `renewed_last:<session>`, written by `./handover`) and the
# round. The state of the snapshot is kept per session
# (`identity_full:<session>`, review I-4): one hive-wide key had two
# sessions take each other's snapshot anew on every call.
SNAPSHOT_KEYS = ("session", "epoch", "renewed", "audience")


def canonical(value):
    """The one serialisation a block is hashed and stored in: keys sorted,
    UTF-8, no whitespace."""
    return json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)


def block_hash(value):
    return hashlib.sha256(canonical(value).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def block_span(text):
    """Where an answer's sidecar block stands: (start, end) or None.

    The boundary is the fence `talky/splitter` cuts (GH #379, #605): the
    ```sidecar fence, or the legacy ```memory fence, to the next closing fence
    or to the end of the text when the completion stopped inside the block.
    Measured, never parsed -- the sections inside are somebody else's business.
    """
    low = text.lower()
    for fence in ("```sidecar", "```memory"):
        at = low.find(fence)
        if at < 0:
            continue
        head = text.find("\n", at)
        close = text.find("```", head + 1) if head >= 0 else -1
        if head >= 0 and close >= 0:
            return at, close + 3
        return at, len(text)
    return None


def stripped_text(text):
    span = block_span(text)
    if span is None:
        return text
    return (text[:span[0]] + text[span[1]:]).strip()


def dropped_text(text, size):
    """An answer whose sidecar block is over its share of the window: the
    answer, and the mark where the block stood (R-IG-1)."""
    bare = stripped_text(text)
    mark = SIDECAR_DROPPED % size
    return (bare + "\n\n" + mark) if bare else mark


def element_of(row):
    """The element a wall row stands for: `element` when the caller has it,
    else the block body the ledger stored."""
    el = row.get("element")
    if isinstance(el, dict):
        return el
    try:
        el = json.loads(str(row.get("body") or ""))
    except Exception:
        return None
    return el if isinstance(el, dict) else None


def plan_cover(plan, cover_rows):
    """Where the window's wall starts: the cover of the current plan, or --
    in a ledger that has none yet -- the newest summary's `covers_to_seq`."""
    if isinstance(plan, dict) and plan.get("cover") is not None:
        try:
            return int(plan.get("cover") or 0)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            pass
    return int((cover_rows[0].get("covers_to_seq") or 0) if cover_rows else 0)


def short_id(h):
    return str(h or "")[:ID_HEX]


def norm_id(value):
    """A block id as a model writes it -- `#0123456789ab`, `[#0123...]`,
    bare -- as its 12 hex digits, or "" when it is none."""
    s = str(value or "").strip().strip("[]").strip().lstrip("#").strip().lower()
    s = s[:12]
    if len(s) != 12 or any(c not in "0123456789abcdef" for c in s):
        return ""
    return s


def epoch_ms(value):
    """A stamped time as epoch milliseconds: RFC 3339 text, or a number of
    seconds (milliseconds above 1e12). None when it reads as neither."""
    if isinstance(value, (int, float)) and not isinstance(value, bool):
        return int(value if value > 1e12 else value * 1000)
    s = str(value or "").strip()
    if not s:
        return None
    try:
        t = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    except ValueError:
        return None
    if t.tzinfo is None:
        t = t.replace(tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
    return int(t.timestamp() * 1000)


def epoch_us(value):
    """A stored stamp as epoch microseconds -- the unit of `wall.seq`, so a
    pin that arrived between two rows stands between them."""
    s = str(value or "").strip()
    try:
        t = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    except ValueError:
        return None
    if t.tzinfo is None:
        t = t.replace(tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
    delta = t - datetime.datetime(1970, 1, 1, tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
    return (delta.days * 86400 + delta.seconds) * 1000000 + delta.microseconds


def prefixable(el):
    """What carries a short id and a one-line form: somebody else's words and
    a tool result (see ID_HEX)."""
    typ = el.get("type")
    return typ == "tool_result" or (typ == "text" and el.get("origin") in ("user", "peer"))


def first_line(text, cap):
    """The first non-empty line of `text`, at most `cap` characters of it --
    a pointer's preview; the form around it says the whole length."""
    for line in str(text or "").splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if line:
            return line if len(line) <= cap else line[:cap].rstrip()
    return ""


def shrunk_form(wid, text):
    """The one-line form of a shortened block: its id, its first line, how many
    characters of how many that line shows, and `history_read` for the rest."""
    head = first_line(text, LINE_CHARS)
    return SHRUNK_FORM % (wid, head, len(head), len(str(text or "")), wid)


def stub_description(text):
    """What a stubbed tool declaration keeps of its description: the first
    line, and when that is not all of it, the mark of `clip` with the whole
    length (R-IG-1)."""
    text = str(text or "")
    head = first_line(text, LINE_CHARS)
    if head == text.strip():
        return head
    return head + "...[cut: %d of %d chars shown; %s]" % (
        len(head), len(text), "the tool is stubbed for the budget of the window")


def expired(el, as_of_ms):
    """A transient block (`valid_until` stamped by whoever made it) whose time
    ran out before the plan was made."""
    until = epoch_ms(el.get("valid_until")) if isinstance(el, dict) else None
    return until is not None and as_of_ms is not None and until <= as_of_ms


# THE GARBAGE COLLECTION OF A REBUILD (GH #1430, R-38-2). Five classes, each a
# whole count in the one `gc` mark of a rebuild: `shrunk_tools` (old tool
# results in their one-line form), `dup_recall` (a recall result whose row a
# younger raw one repeats), `scaffold` (the inner rows of a closed
# delegation), `released` (what the model released), `transient` (what ran
# out). Never an error result, never the person's words; every form keeps the
# way back (`history_read`).
GC_CLASSES = ("shrunk_tools", "dup_recall", "transient", "released", "scaffold")
SCAFFOLD_KINDS = ("advice", "delegation")


def recall_row(line):
    """True for a row of a recall result in the form the memory hive renders
    it (`render_payload_lines`, GH #281): a line at an indent of exactly two
    that is no parenthesised caveat. The document head, the section heads and
    the notes above them stand unindented, the caveats at two in parentheses,
    a reply under a fact at four -- review I-1 of GH #1430: hashing those
    made two results without a fact in common duplicates and counted seven
    rows for three (OR-d38-1.k3.12). The shape, never the words."""
    if not line.startswith("  ") or line[2:3] in ("", " ", "\t"):
        return False
    body = line.rstrip()
    return not (body[2:].startswith("(") and body.endswith(")"))


def row_lines(text):
    """The canonical hashes of the rows (`recall_row`) of a recall result
    (class `dup_recall`, `recall_rows`): the row stripped, sha256 of its
    UTF-8, the first 16 hex -- a row is the same row by its bytes, never by
    resemblance."""
    if RECALL_IN_WALL:
        # GH #1463: a quote over several lines is one row (`recall_rows`), so
        # the rows a rebuild compares are the rows the window decides on.
        # Behind the knob: `dup_recall` reads these hashes with `gc` on, and a
        # hive that never turned `recall_in_wall` on keeps its rebuilds.
        return [hashlib.sha256(row.strip().encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]
                for row in recall_rows(text)]
    return [hashlib.sha256(line.strip().encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]
            for line in str(text or "").splitlines() if recall_row(line)]


# GH #1463: where a quote of a recall row ends -- the closing mark and, behind
# it, only what the memory hive hangs on a row (its annotations, each a space
# and a group in round or square brackets: ` (seen: 2)`, ` [<from> -> <to>]`).
QUOTE_END = re.compile(r'"(?: \([^\n]*\)| \[[^\n]*\])*\s*$')


def recall_rows(text):
    """The rows of a recall result with a quote over several lines as ONE row
    (GH #1463). The memory hive renders a text with line breaks as a head row
    with the opening mark, the further lines without an indent (blank ones
    too), and the closing mark with the annotations on the last. A head row
    with one quote mark only takes the lines behind it up to the first that
    ends on a mark (`QUOTE_END`), joined by a line feed; without such a line
    it stays the row it was. Kalibrierung d58-2 (reader note v5m): judged line
    by line, the head row was no quote and no block of an answer with a list
    ever left -- the bulk of the doubled recall blocks of the S8 run."""
    lines = str(text or "").splitlines()
    out, i = [], 0
    while i < len(lines):
        line = lines[i]
        i += 1
        if not recall_row(line):
            continue
        row = line.strip()
        a = row.find('"')
        if a >= 0 and row.count('"') == 1 and (not row[:a] or row[:a].endswith(": ")):
            j = i
            while j < len(lines) and not QUOTE_END.search(lines[j]):
                j += 1
            if j < len(lines):
                row = "\n".join([line.lstrip()] + lines[i:j + 1])
                i = j + 1
        out.append(row)
    return out


def recall_quotes(text):
    """The hashes (`said_hash` form) of the quotes of the recall result
    `text`, one per row (`recall_rows`): a row is a quote `<who>: "<words>"`
    (or `"<words>"`), its words first mark to last -- for a row of several
    lines to the closing mark `QUOTE_END` finds, so an annotation behind it
    is no part of the words. None when the result has no row or one row is no
    such quote."""
    out = []
    for row in recall_rows(text):
        a = row.find('"')
        head = row[:a]
        if "\n" in row:
            m = QUOTE_END.search(row)
            b = m.start() if m else -1
        else:
            b = row.rfind('"')
        if a < 0 or b <= a or (head and not head.endswith(": ")):
            return None
        out.append(hashlib.sha256(row[a + 1:b].strip().encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16])
    return out or None


def said_hash(el):
    """The hash a recall quote must equal for the raw user/assistant element
    `el` (`said_hashes`), None for any other element."""
    if not (isinstance(el, dict) and el.get("type", "text") == "text"
            and el.get("origin") in ("user", "assistant")):
        return None
    return hashlib.sha256(stripped_text(str(el.get("text") or "")).strip().encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]


def said_hashes(els):
    """The `row_lines` hashes of the texts of the raw user/assistant elements
    `els` -- what a recall quote must equal to stand in the wall (V5).

    GH #1458: the words without the answer's sidecar block (`stripped_text`,
    the boundary `talky/splitter` cuts): the memory hive quotes the spoken
    words only. Hashed raw, no assistant quote ever matched, and in the S8
    run every doubled recall block stayed (100 %; reader note leser-v5: k10
    0 of 10 recall blocks cut, 6 with the strip; k30 0 of 29, 24)."""
    return set(hashlib.sha256(stripped_text(str(el.get("text") or "")).strip().encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]
               for el in els if isinstance(el, dict) and el.get("type", "text") == "text"
               and el.get("origin") in ("user", "assistant"))


def recall_in_wall(text, wall_hashes):
    """D38 V5 (OR-38-84 b): True when every row (`recall_row`) of the recall
    result `text` is a quote `<who>: "<words>"` (or `"<words>"`) whose words,
    first to last quote mark, hash (`row_lines` form) to a raw element of the
    window in `wall_hashes`. No row, or one row without such a quote, is
    False: the block stays. GH #1463: a quote over several lines is one row
    and is compared whole (`recall_quotes`)."""
    quotes = recall_quotes(text)
    return bool(quotes) and all(h in wall_hashes for h in quotes)


def closed_round(turn, as_of_ms):
    """True for the turn of an inner round (`round_label`) whose deadline
    (`round_deadline`, the `until` of its `pending:delegation:` row) lies at
    or before `as_of_ms`: the errand is over (OR-d38-1.k3.2)."""
    deadline = round_deadline(turn)
    return bool(round_label(turn)) and 0 < deadline and as_of_ms is not None \
        and deadline <= int(as_of_ms)


def shrinkable(r, el):
    """What the window may show in its one-line form when a plan shrank it: a
    tool result that is no error (GH #1430 -- a plan from before may name one),
    or the scaffold of a closed delegation."""
    if el.get("type") == "tool_result":
        return not result_failed(r, el)
    return str(r.get("kind") or "") in SCAFFOLD_KINDS


def sent_chars(r, gone):
    """The characters a wall row is sent at (GH #1434, review M-2): a row
    whose short id is in `gone` (`gone_ids`: shrunk, released or expired by
    the plan, which `render` shows in its one-line form) at FORM_CHARS, a
    final answer `render` cuts at its sidecar block (`with_cut`) at the
    characters of the cut text, every other at its block's characters. The
    one row rule of the raw budget and the `curate` stamp (`raw_estimate`),
    the plan's `estimate` and the `gc` mark's `tool_share`; before, each of
    them spelled it out."""
    if short_id(r.get("hash")) in gone:
        return FORM_CHARS
    cut = r.get("cut_chars")
    return int(cut) if cut is not None else int(r.get("chars") or 0)


def gone_ids(rows, shrunk, released, as_of_ms, current=None):
    """The short ids of the rows a plan sends in a one-line form (GH #1434,
    review m-2): `shrunk`, `released`, and every row of `rows` whose transient
    block ran out at or before `as_of_ms` (`expired`; `render` shows it as
    `EXPIRED_FORM`). A row carries `valid_until` itself (a rebuild's
    enriched wall) or in its element (the wall of a call). The one set the
    raw budget, its cap at the aim, the plan's `estimate`, the `gc` mark and
    the `curate` stamp hand `sent_chars`; before, the budget and the stamp
    each built it and the estimate left the expired rows out (review I-1':
    the cap at the aim counted them at their form, the estimate whole, and a
    plan that fit as sent was said over the aim). `current`, the running
    round `(session_id, turn_id)`: `render` sends its rows whole (`key !=
    current`), so a row only of it is never in the set -- an expired or
    released row of the running round counted at its form and went out
    whole, and the budget filled older rounds on top of it (rest list of the
    review of GH #1434)."""
    out = set(shrunk or ()) | set(released or ())
    if as_of_ms is not None:
        for r in rows:
            if r.get("valid_until") is not None:
                el = r
            elif r.get("element") is not None or r.get("body") is not None:
                el = element_of(r)
            else:
                continue
            if expired(el, as_of_ms):
                out.add(short_id(r.get("hash")))
    if current is not None:
        mine, others = set(), set()
        for r in rows:
            key = (str(r.get("session_id") or ""), str(r.get("turn_id") or ""))
            (mine if key == current else others).add(short_id(r.get("hash")))
        out -= mine - others
    return out


def sidecar_cut(row, el, cap):
    """The text a final answer of the model is sent at when its sidecar block
    is over `cap` characters (`render`, GH #871, R-IG-1) and the size of the
    block, `(text, size)`; None when it goes whole (no cap, no block, another
    row). The one rule of `render` and of the rows the raw budget and the
    `curate` stamp measure (`with_cut`, GH #1434: they counted the whole
    block, and the stamp could pass the call's own projection)."""
    if cap is None or el is None:
        return None
    if str(row.get("kind") or "") != "assistant" or int(row.get("final") or 0) != 1:
        return None
    text = str(el.get("text") or "")
    span = block_span(text)
    if span is None or span[1] - span[0] <= cap:
        return None
    size = span[1] - span[0]
    return dropped_text(text, size), size


def with_cut(row, el, cap):
    """`row` with `cut_chars`, the characters `render` sends of its cut
    answer (`sidecar_cut`), when it cuts one; else `row` itself."""
    cut = sidecar_cut(row, el, cap)
    return dict(row, cut_chars=len(cut[0])) if cut is not None else row


def gc_figure(rows, cover, keep, gone, classes, total_chars):
    """The value of the `gc` mark of a plan (without its call): the counts per
    class, `tool_share` -- the characters of the tool results the window keeps
    above the cover (a one-line form at `FORM_CHARS`) over all the estimate
    counts --, and `recall_rows`, the rows of the newest recall result that
    stays raw (OR-d38-1.k3.6). `gone` is the plan's `gone_ids`."""
    tools, recall = 0, None
    keep = set(keep)
    out = set(gone)
    for r in rows:
        s = int(r["seq"])
        if s <= cover and s not in keep:
            continue
        if r.get("type") == "tool_result":
            tools += sent_chars(r, out)
            if r.get("recall") and short_id(r.get("hash")) not in out:
                recall = r
    share = round(min(1.0, float(tools) / total_chars), 4) if total_chars > 0 else 0.0
    return {"classes": dict((c, int(classes.get(c) or 0)) for c in GC_CLASSES),
            "tool_share": share,
            "recall_rows": len((recall or {}).get("lines") or [])}


def raw_estimate(rows, gone, rate):
    """Tokens of `rows` as the window sends them (GH #1434): a row whose short
    id is in `gone` (shrunk or released by the plan) at FORM_CHARS, every
    other at its block's characters, over `rate` -- the one figure the raw
    budget (`keep_recent_tokens`) fills and the `curate` stamp names
    (`raw_tokens`). Before, the budget counted the rows before the garbage
    collection (a knob of 20000 left about 11000 raw tokens in the window) and
    the stamp `estimate_tokens` of their elements (about 1.37x the budget)."""
    return sum(sent_chars(r, gone) for r in rows) / rate


# THE MODEL'S RELEASES PER AUDIENCE (GH #932, review I-1). A release or a pin
# the model says is a `marks` row of the round it was said in; a rebuild
# reads only the marks its own round may see. The plan keeps what each
# audience said last about a block -- `marks_on[id][audience] = [group_seq,
# rank, seq, kind]` -- so a mark is never lost when a rebuild of another
# round runs, and it shapes only the windows of rounds that may see it.
def round_canon(round_value):
    """The canonical round: `"[]"` for none -- what `marks_on` and
    `marks_to_by` are keyed by. (`round_key` until GH #943, which gave that
    name to the short key of the state.)"""
    return audience_of(round_value) or "[]"


def round_key(round_value):
    """The key a round's state is kept under (GH #943): the first 12 hex
    digits of the sha256 of its canonical form (`round_canon`). The same
    round in another order or with duplicates is the same key; a round
    nobody declared has the key of `[]`; `["*"]` is a round of its own. A
    hash and not the canonical text: a `state` key stays short and plain
    whatever the round names. `./intake` keeps the same formula (OR-BC.W.1)."""
    return hashlib.sha256(round_canon(round_value).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:12]


# The key of the round this message serves (GH #943): the suffix of every
# state key that is kept per round. Here and not beside `the_round`, because
# `round_key` is defined only now; lower case for the same reason as
# `the_round` (the pure half is loaded with the upper-case constants only).
the_rk = round_key(the_round)


def rkey(name, rk=None):
    """A state key of one round (GH #943): `<name>:<rk>`, this message's
    round unless `rk` names another."""
    return "%s:%s" % (name, the_rk if rk is None else rk)


def newest_slots(rows):
    """One `slots` row per path, as a PURE function (GH #1225, K-4): the
    newest by `at`, on a tie the smallest `hash` -- an explicit order, since
    the store's select names none and `rowid` is not readable through it. A
    row without a readable `at` is the oldest. Paths keep the order of their
    first row. Why: `slots` had no key on `path`, and two writes in flight
    left copies of one path (the review measured 21 copies of one path in 4
    versions); every reader counted each -- the window estimate, the leaves
    sent and `call_blocks` 21 times."""
    best, order = {}, []
    for r in rows:
        path = str(r.get("path") or "")
        at = epoch_us(r.get("at"))
        rank = (at if at is not None else -1, str(r.get("hash") or ""))
        cur = best.get(path)
        if cur is None:
            order.append(path)
        elif not (rank[0] > cur[0][0] or (rank[0] == cur[0][0] and rank[1] < cur[0][1])):
            continue
        best[path] = (rank, r)
    return [best[p][1] for p in order]


def own_slots(rows, rk, newest=True):
    """The `slots` rows as the round `rk` sees them (GH #943, OR-BC.W.2), as a
    PURE function: the summary slot of a round is the row
    `history.summary:<rk>`, shown as the leaf `history.summary`; the slot of
    another round and a bare `history.summary` row (from before the rule, not
    moved) are left out; every other row stays as it is. Why: with one
    summary slot per hive, the rebuild of one round replaced or deleted the
    summary leaf of another. One row per path (`newest_slots`, GH #1225) --
    `newest=False` only for a read that fetches blocks and counts nothing
    (`win-hashes`: `./intake` hands its slot hashes on without `at`, and the
    block of the newest copy has to come along whichever copy that is)."""
    out = []
    for r in (newest_slots(rows) if newest else rows):
        path = str(r.get("path") or "")
        if path == SUMMARY_PATH:
            continue
        if path.startswith(SUMMARY_PATH + ":"):
            if path != SUMMARY_PATH + ":" + rk:
                continue
            r = dict(r, path=SUMMARY_PATH)
        out.append(r)
    return out


def prune_plans(reg, rk, now_ms_value, max_plans, idle_s):
    """The registry of a hive's round plans after a rebuild of the round
    `rk` (GH #943), as a PURE function: `reg` maps a round key to the epoch
    ms of its last rebuild. `rk` is stamped `now_ms_value`; every other round
    idle for more than `idle_s` seconds goes, and then, while more than
    `max_plans` are left, the oldest (the smallest stamp, on a tie the
    smallest key) -- never `rk` itself. Returns `(new_reg, dropped)`, the
    dropped keys sorted. Why: a plan per round is a state row per round, and
    rounds come and go; "used" is the last rebuild, since a window without
    one lives no longer than the provider's cache."""
    out = {}
    for k, t in (reg or {}).items():
        try:
            out[str(k)] = int(t)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            # A stamp nobody can read is as old as it gets.
            out[str(k)] = 0
    out[rk] = int(now_ms_value)
    dropped = [k for k, t in out.items()
               if k != rk and int(now_ms_value) - t > idle_s * 1000]
    for k in dropped:
        del out[k]
    while len(out) > max_plans:
        rest = sorted((t, k) for k, t in out.items() if k != rk)
        if not rest:
            break
        dropped.append(rest[0][1])
        del out[rest[0][1]]
    return out, sorted(dropped)


def mark_applies(rk, aud):
    """Whether what the audience `aud` said holds for the round `rk`: the
    gate (`allowed`); for a round-less round (`"[]"`) only a round-less or a
    `*` audience, as `passes` lets a round-less read see only those rows --
    `allowed` would let every declared audience hold for an empty round."""
    if rk == "[]":
        a = audience_of(aud)
        return a is not None and (a == "[]" or "*" in json.loads(a))
    return allowed(rk, aud)


def marks_on_of(prev):
    """The `marks_on` a plan carries, or -- for a plan from before it -- its
    `released` as said by everybody, before any mark of this plan."""
    prev = prev if isinstance(prev, dict) else {}
    if isinstance(prev.get("marks_on"), dict):
        return dict((str(i), dict(v)) for i, v in prev["marks_on"].items() if isinstance(v, dict))
    return dict((str(i), {"[\"*\"]": [0, 0, 0, "release"]}) for i in (prev.get("released") or []))


def released_in(marks_on, rk):
    """The ids released for the round `rk`: those whose newest entry that
    holds for `rk` is a release."""
    out = set()
    for i, by in (marks_on or {}).items():
        best = None
        for aud, entry in (by or {}).items():
            if isinstance(entry, list) and len(entry) == 4 and mark_applies(rk, aud) \
                    and (best is None or entry > best):
                best = entry
        if best is not None and best[3] == "release":
            out.add(i)
    return out


# THE PLAN OF BUILDING BLOCKS (GH #1448, D38 C2, R-38-4 Nr. 2). Stage 1 of the
# curator: the window is a list of blocks `{id, kind, prio, origin, tokens,
# audience, valid_until}` kept in the round's plan (`window_plan:<rk>`, the one
# plan form: `blocks` and `blocks_to` beside the rebuild's keys), written after
# each answer (`tap`) and by a rebuild; a turn appends its new blocks only.
# Model free: `tokens` is the neutral estimate (`estimate_tokens`, three bytes
# a token) -- never a catalog row's `chars_per_token`, never `input_soft`
# (stage 2 sizes per target model). `prio` comes from the knob `block_prio`
# (kind -> whole number, R-IG-1); a kind it does not name has its `default`.
BLOCK_PLAN_KEYS = ("blocks", "blocks_to", "left_out", "ahead")
# GH #1463, written only with `recall_in_wall` on (`left_out` also with
# `recall_skip_sure`, GH #1466): `left_out`, the wall hashes
# of the recall pairs a call decided to leave out (no later call takes them up
# again, a rebuild carries the list on), and `ahead`, the wall hashes of the
# blocks the tap planned ahead of the wall (checked once by the next call). A
# recall block that was decided and stayed says `decided` "kept" itself.


def block_prio_table(raw):
    """`block_prio` as kind -> whole number, from a JSON text or an object; a
    value that is no whole number is left out."""
    v = raw
    if not isinstance(v, dict):
        try:
            v = json.loads(str(raw or ""))
        except ValueError:
            v = {}
    v = v if isinstance(v, dict) else {}
    return {str(k): x for k, x in v.items() if isinstance(x, int) and not isinstance(x, bool)}


BLOCK_PRIO = block_prio_table(P.get("block_prio"))


# GH #1469: the outcome of an errand stays like a tool result that failed --
# a table that does not name the kind gives it the prio of `tool_result`.
PRIO_LIKE = {"outcome": "tool_result"}


def prio_of(kind):
    return int(BLOCK_PRIO.get(kind, BLOCK_PRIO.get(PRIO_LIKE.get(kind),
                                                   BLOCK_PRIO.get("default", 0))))


def rebuilt_part(plan):
    """The plan without its blocks: what a rebuild made (cover, keep, summary,
    ...). Every step that reads the rebuild's keys reads this, so a plan of
    blocks only reads as no plan -- the window of before, byte for byte."""
    plan = plan if isinstance(plan, dict) else {}
    return {k: v for k, v in plan.items() if k not in BLOCK_PLAN_KEYS}


# OR-d38-3.o10.2 (review I1): the pairs `./push` hands `./intake` -- a gap's
# find and the candidates -- are push lines, whatever their ledger kind.
PUSH_IDS = ("call_addendum_", "call_candidates_")


def block_kind(el, wall_kind=""):
    """The kind of the block of the wall element `el` (its ledger kind beside)."""
    t = str(el.get("type") or "")
    if t in ("tool_call", "tool_result") and str(el.get("id") or "").startswith(PUSH_IDS):
        return "push"
    if t == "tool_result":
        amb = ambient_of(el)
        if wall_kind == "recall" or amb == "recall":
            return "recall"
        return "brief" if amb == "brief" else "tool_result"
    if t == "tool_call":
        return "tool_call"
    if wall_kind in SCAFFOLD_KINDS:
        return "note"
    if wall_kind == OUTCOME_KIND:
        # GH #1469: a kind of its own -- no scaffold, nobody's words.
        return OUTCOME_KIND
    return "answer" if str(el.get("origin") or "") == "assistant" else "words"


def block_of(kind, el, origin, audience, valid_until=None):
    """One block: id `<kind>:<12 hex of its origin>` (OR-d38-3.c2.1)."""
    h = str(origin.get("hash") or "") or block_hash(origin)
    return {"id": "%s:%s" % (kind, short_id(h)), "kind": kind, "prio": prio_of(kind),
            "origin": origin, "tokens": int(estimate_tokens(el)), "audience": audience,
            "valid_until": valid_until}


def rebuild_blocks(plan, rows, blocks, audience):
    """GH #1448 (Z1.6): the blocks of the plan a rebuild made -- the wall rows
    its window still shows (over `cover`, or kept), a released, shortened or
    run-out one as a `stub`, in seq order; the condensate is `with_brief`'s."""
    cover = int(plan.get("cover") or 0)
    keep = set(int(x) for x in (plan.get("keep") or []) if str(x).lstrip("-").isdigit())
    released, shrunk = set(plan.get("released") or []), set(plan.get("shrunk") or [])
    out, seen = [], set()
    rows = sorted(rows, key=lambda r: int(r.get("seq") or 0))
    # GH #1463: a rebuild decides every recall block of an earlier round that
    # it leaves in the plan -- with the collection on (`gc`) it checked the
    # block against the wall (`gc_shrink`), with it off it checked nothing
    # and the block stays as it is. Either way no later call checks the
    # block again: what was sent stays until a rebuild clears it. The block
    # of the newest round is decided by the call after its round.
    newest = (str(rows[-1].get("session_id") or ""), str(rows[-1].get("turn_id") or "")) \
        if rows and RECALL_IN_WALL else None
    for r in rows:
        seq, h = int(r.get("seq") or 0), str(r.get("hash") or "")
        el = element_of(blocks.get(h) or {})
        if el is None or (seq <= cover and seq not in keep):
            continue
        wid = short_id(h)
        # Z1.9: every class of the garbage collection marks its block -- a
        # released, a shortened and a run-out one (`transient`) is a stub.
        gone = wid in released or (wid in shrunk and shrinkable(r, el)) \
            or (seq > cover and expired(el, plan.get("as_of_ms")))
        kind = "stub" if gone else block_kind(el, str(r.get("kind") or ""))
        b = block_of(kind, el, {"source": "wall", "hash": h}, audience, el.get("valid_until"))
        if newest is not None and kind == "recall" \
                and (str(r.get("session_id") or ""), str(r.get("turn_id") or "")) != newest:
            b["decided"] = "kept"
        if b["id"] not in seen:
            seen.add(b["id"])
            out.append(b)
    return out


def with_brief(plan, h, el, audience):
    """GH #1448 (Z1.6): the plan with its condensate as one `brief` block in
    front (origin the summary block `h`), none when the plan holds no
    summary; the brief of before goes."""
    rest = [b for b in plan.get("blocks") or []
            if (b.get("origin") or {}).get("source") != "summary"]
    if plan.get("summary") and h:
        rest = [block_of("brief", el or {}, {"source": "summary", "hash": h}, audience)] + rest
    return dict(plan, blocks=rest)


def blocks_of_rows(rows, have, audience):
    """The blocks of the wall rows `rows` (each with its `body` or element
    `el`), in their order, but for the ids in `have` (a row already planned)."""
    out, seen = [], set(have)
    for r in rows:
        el = r.get("el")
        if not isinstance(el, dict):
