        # GH #1225 (A3): the claim or the answer is out of reach -- read as
        # empty, the claim stayed held until it went stale. It is freed by its
        # token (the reason, as from `rb-claim` on); the parked answer waits
        # for the sweep.
        release_refused(lg, phase, reason)
    state = state_of(lg, "s-read")
    raw = state.get(rkey("rebuild_running"), "")
    info = loads(raw, {})
    if claim_wall(info):
        (KEEP_RECENT, KEEP_RECENT_TOKENS, COMPRESS_AT, REBUILD_TO, HORIZON, TIERS, KEEP_ROUNDS,
     GC, GC_SCAFFOLD, STUB_TOOLS_AFTER, WINDOW_TARGET, STATE_LINES) = wall_values(claim_wall(info))
    payload = loads(state.get(rkey("pending:summary"), ""), {})
    drop = ("s-drop", {"operation": "delete", "table": "state",
                       "where": {"key": rkey("pending:summary")}})
    if not info.get("sources"):
        emit([lstore([drop], "done", call, reason)])
    if not reason or reason != str(info.get("token") or ""):
        # An answer asked for under ANOTHER claim (review M-10, R2-I-14): a
        # rebuild whose claim went stale (REBUILD_STALE_S) answers while the
        # next one holds the lock. Kept, the words of the round the old
        # transcript was made for would stand under the new claim's sources
        # and audience; it is dropped, and the running claim waits for its
        # own answer.
        sys.stderr.write("curator/policy: a summary asked for under another claim"
                         " -- dropped (GH #925)\n")
        emit([lstore([drop], "done", call, reason)])
    pending_actions = state.get(rkey("actions_pending"), "")
    text = str(payload.get("text") or "")
    why = str(info.get("reason") or reason or "cache")
    failure = ""
    brief_marks = []
    if payload.get("finish") != "stop":
        failure = "finish_reason %s %s" % (payload.get("finish") or "?",
                                          payload.get("error_code") or "")
    elif not text.strip():
        failure = "an empty summary"
    elif info.get("form") == "brief":
        # GH #1440 (OR-38-42, OR-d38-2.z3.6): only lines of the form stay;
        # none -- the old window stays -- or some dropped, the mark says it.
        new, dropped = brief_lines(text, transcript_days(info.get("transcript")),
                                   transcript_ids(info.get("transcript")))
        if dropped:
            mstamp = now()
            brief_marks.append(("s-rej", ins("marks", with_audience({
                "seq": epoch_us(mstamp), "session_id": str(info.get("session") or ""),
                "turn_id": "", "kind": "summary_rejected",
                "value": canonical({"kept": len(new), "dropped": dropped}),
                "at": mstamp}, the_round))))
        if not new:
            failure = "summary_rejected: no line of the form"
        else:
            srcs = info.get("sources") or []
            text = brief_render(brief_merge(brief_lines(info.get("prev_text")
                                                        or info.get("carry_text"))[0],
                                            brief_point(new, srcs, srcs[-1] if srcs else ""))[0])
    if not failure:
        leaf = (SUMMARY_HEAD % (int(info.get("shown_to") or 0), info.get("first_at") or "?",
                                info.get("last_at") or "?") + "\n" + text)
        size = len(json.dumps({"text": leaf}, ensure_ascii=False,
                              separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8"))
        if size > LEAF_MAX_BYTES:
            failure = "too_long: %d > %d bytes" % (size, LEAF_MAX_BYTES)
    if not failure and payload.get("self"):
        # GH #1440 (OR-38-42 A1): one ledger mark per summary the role's own
        # model wrote (`summarizer_self`), past the seq of `summary_rejected`.
        mstamp = now()
        brief_marks.append(("s-self", ins("marks", with_audience({
            "seq": epoch_us(mstamp) + 1, "session_id": str(info.get("session") or ""),
            "turn_id": "", "kind": "summary_self",
            "value": canonical(dict(payload.get("tokens") or {}, call=call, why=why,
                                    model=str(payload.get("model") or ""))),
            "at": mstamp}, the_round))))
    if failure:
        # OR-KX-K6: the window stays what it was; the next call says so.
        emit([lstore(old_window_kept(raw, pending_actions, why, failure, state) + brief_marks
                     + [drop],
                     "done", call, reason)])
    stamp = now()
    summary = {"type": "summary", "text": text}
    h = block_hash(summary)
    sid = str(uuid.uuid4())
    covers = int(info.get("covers_to_seq") or 0)
    # The head names what went in (review M-1); the row keeps the plan's cover.
    shown = int(info.get("shown_to") or 0)
    rendered = (SUMMARY_HEAD % (shown, info.get("first_at") or "?", info.get("last_at") or "?")
                + "\n" + text)
    slot_el = {"path": SUMMARY_PATH, "text": rendered}
    sh = block_hash(slot_el)
    ops = [block_put("s-b1", h, "summary", len(text), canonical(summary), stamp),
           block_put("s-b2", sh, "system", len(rendered), canonical(slot_el), stamp),
           # GH #925 (OR-BD-3): the summary reaches a round only where every
           # source it was made of would have -- the meet `rb-data` noted.
           ("s-row", ins("summaries", with_meet({
               "id": sid, "covers_to_seq": covers, "hash": h,
               "sources": info.get("sources") or [],
               "model": str(payload.get("model") or ""), "at": stamp}, info.get("audience"))))]
    # The round's own slot `history.summary:<rk>` (GH #943, OR-BC.W.2); its
    # block is the leaf `history.summary` the window shows (`own_slots`).
    # One write whatever the claim read (`slot_put`, GH #1225).
    ops.append(slot_put("s-slot", rkey(SUMMARY_PATH), sh, stamp))
    # The summary leaf's audience, bound to the leaf's hash and PUT whole
    # beside the slot (review R2-I-4): the store does not roll a failed leg
    # back, so read off the newest `summaries` row, a bundle whose slot leg
    # failed left the old summary under the new one's audience, and one whose
    # row leg failed left the new summary under the old one's -- the window
    # shows the leaf only where this hash is the slot's.
    ops += put("s-aud", rkey("summary_audience"), canonical(
        {"audience": info.get("audience"), "hash": sh}))
    result = dict(info.get("result") or {})
    result["plan"] = with_brief(dict(result.get("plan") or {}, summary=sid, sum_shown=shown),
                                h, summary, round_canon(the_round))
    ops = finish(info, result, why, pending_actions, raw, stamp, ops + brief_marks,
                 ["summary:" + sid], state=state)
    emit([lstore(ops + [drop], "done", call, reason)])

if phase == "dlg-park" and ERRAND_OUTCOME:
    # Wave d58-2 close (inventory 39, errand review M1, first gap): the park
    # of a delegation round, written only while none stood. Taken, or the row
    # that stands is this round's own (a round delivered again): nothing more.
    # Another errand's row stands -- a second errand of the same turn: it
    # stays, and this round's errand leaves the mark `errand_outcome`
    # "not followed" (once per round, `if_absent`) beside the first's id.
    # Nothing tracks its end; the mark says so instead of a silent overwrite.
    report_errors(lg)
    if failed_legs(lg) or (lg.get("f-dlg") or {}).get("rows_affected", 0) > 0:
        emit([])
    meta = loads(reason, {})
    d_key, d_turn = str(meta.get("k") or ""), str(meta.get("t") or "")
    d_row = loads(state_of(lg, "f-dlgr").get(d_key, ""), {})
    if not d_key or not d_turn or not isinstance(d_row, dict) \
            or not d_row.get("delegation_id") or str(d_row.get("round") or "") == d_turn:
        emit([])
    stamp = now()
    d_mark = ins("marks", with_audience({
        "seq": (epoch_us(stamp) or 0) + 15, "session_id": str(meta.get("s") or ""),
        "turn_id": d_turn, "kind": OUTCOME_MARK,
        "value": canonical({"delegation_id": str(meta.get("id") or ""),
                            "outcome": OUTCOME_UNFOLLOWED,
                            "followed": str(d_row.get("delegation_id") or "")}),
        "at": stamp}, the_round))
    d_mark["if_absent"] = {"turn_id": d_turn, "kind": OUTCOME_MARK}
    emit([lstore([("eo-nf", d_mark)], "done", call, "")])

if phase == "errand-end":
    # GH #1469: the parked row of the errand whose round a tap heard end,
    # as the store holds it now -- written back with the end added, by the
    # value read: a row parked anew, swept or changed since stays as it is.
    # The row of another errand of the same turn (its `round` differs) is
    # not this one's.
    report_errors(lg)
    meta = loads(reason, {})
    e_key = str(meta.get("k") or "")
    e_raw = state_of(lg, "eo-row").get(e_key, "")
    e_row = loads(e_raw, {})
    if failed_legs(lg) or not e_row.get("delegation_id") \
            or str(e_row.get("round") or "") != str(meta.get("t") or ""):
        emit([])
    e_new = errand_ended(e_row, str(meta.get("end") or ""), meta.get("code"))
    if e_new == e_row:
        emit([])
    # Wave d58-2 close (inventory 39, errand review M1): the write is a step
    # of its own (`errand-put`), so a compare-and-set that took nothing is
    # seen and the row is read again.
    emit([lstore([("eo-put", upd("state", {"value": canonical(e_new)},
                                 {"key": e_key, "value": e_raw}))], "errand-put", call, reason)])

if phase == "errand-put":
    # Wave d58-2 close (inventory 39, errand review M1): the compare-and-set
    # of `errand-end` took nothing -- another writer changed the row between
    # its read and this write (an earlier call of the round, a curate filing
    # an outcome). Lost, an `answered` read as `no answer` past the deadline,
    # beside the answer. The row is read again and the end added to what
    # stands (`errand-end`). Every retry follows a write of someone else, so
    # the chain ends: the write took, or the row went, or it holds the end.
    report_errors(lg)
    e_put = lg.get("eo-put") or {}
    if failed_legs(lg) or e_put.get("rows_affected", 0) > 0:
        emit([])
    e_key = str(loads(reason, {}).get("k") or "")
    if not e_key:
        emit([])
    emit([lstore([("eo-row", sel("state", ["key", "value"], {"key": e_key}))],
                 "errand-end", call, reason)])

if phase == "swept":
    # A13: the parked rows past their age are down (or were parked anew, or
    # another cell swept them first). The mark names the rows that went; a
    # refused delete is said as a `store_error` mark beside it. The answer to
    # those marks comes back here without keys and ends the chain.
    report_errors(lg)
    sweep = loads(reason, {}) if ERRAND_OUTCOME else {}
    keys = sweep.get("keys") if sweep else loads(reason, [])
    keys = [str(k) for k in keys] if isinstance(keys, list) else []
    ops = swept_mark(lg, keys) if keys else []
    if sweep:
        # GH #1469 (OR-d58-2.errand.14): the errands whose row went have
        # their outcome filed now, in the bundle of the mark.
        ops += swept_outcomes(lg, keys, sweep)
    q_failed = failed_legs(lg, ["q-d%d" % i for i in range(len(keys))])
    if q_failed:
        ops.append(store_error_mark("q-err", phase, q_failed))
    o_failed = dict((cid, code) for cid, code in failed_legs(lg).items()
                    if cid.startswith(OUTCOME_LEGS))
    if o_failed:
        # Wave d58-2 close (inventory 42, errand review m1, OR-d58-2.errand.18):
        # the store refused the outcome of an errand whose row the sweep
        # already took -- no later sweep or curate files it again. The loss
        # stands in the ledger as a `store_error` mark, as a refused delete's
        # does (GH #1225), not on stderr alone. Its answer carries no outcome
        # leg and ends the chain.
        ops.append(store_error_mark("q-oerr", phase, o_failed))
    if ops:
        emit([lstore(ops, "swept", call, "")])
    emit([])

park("store answer in unknown phase %r -- dropped" % phase)

recall_by_needs.description: GH #1441 (RK-38-7, OR-38-2), GH #1448 (OR-38-65 b): `1` or true = a brain call of a stamped turn whose route stamp does not name `memory` in `needs` lowers the prio of the running round's recall block to `block_prio.recall_unneeded`; the recall stays in the window whole -- never dropped for the stamp alone, stage 2 cuts it first under budget pressure. A `talk` turn whose stamp is a fallback (`hop.fallback`) keeps its prio (A11), so does a turn without a path; the collector carries `hop.fallback` only with its knob `needs_no_recall` on, so switch both together. Only the running round on the `brain` way. `0` (the default) = the window of before.

recall_in_wall.description: D38 V5 (GH #1451), D58 (GH #1463): 1 = stage 1 decides on a recall block once, at the first call after its round: a block whose every row quotes a raw user/assistant turn of the window the call sends (sha256 of the bytes, a quote over several lines whole) is left out with its tool_call -- said on the hop, in the snapshot (`sent`: form `cut` with `why`) and in the plan (`left_out`) -- and no later call cuts it again; any other block stays (`decided` at the block) until a rebuild collects it (class `dup_recall`). The recall of the running round stays. 0 (shipped) = the window and the plan of before.

recall_skip_sure.description: D58 (GH #1466): 1 = the recall the collector fetched for the running turn is left out of the window when the turn's route stamp surely says the turn needs no memory: the stamp is judged (a path, no `fallback`), `memory` is not among its `needs`, and the yes-value of the memory question (`needs_yes.memory` on the seam, sent by a route cell with `stamp_needs_yes` on) is at most `recall_skip_max_yes`. Decided once, when the pair arrives and before it was ever sent: the pair goes whole, the plan keeps the decision (`left_out`), no later call or rebuild takes the block up again. Said on the hop (cut `recall_skip_sure`), as one mark `recall_skipped` (`{block, call, yes}`) and in the snapshot (`sent`: form `cut` with `why`). No stamp, a late one (the pair already left with a call), a fallback, no readable yes-value: the block stays. A `memory_recall` the model called itself is never touched. The lookup itself still runs; the rule saves window, not the lookup. 0 (shipped) = the window and the plan of before.

recall_skip_max_yes.description: D58 (GH #1466): the highest yes-value of the route stamp's memory question at which `recall_skip_sure` still calls the turn sure (inclusive), a number from 0 to 1. A set takes it from its own measurement; a value that is no number from 0 to 1 means never sure. Read only with `recall_skip_sure` on.

keep_recent.description: How many of the newest rounds (one session and turn each) a rebuild leaves raw, whatever their segment's tier. Preset: 12 without a role, talky 40, consult 10, coding 20, research 10. Numeric strings are read as numbers.

keep_recent_tokens.description: GH #1427: the raw token budget -- the youngest rounds whose estimated size together is at most this many tokens stay raw, across session and day boundaries, never below `keep_recent` rounds, never above the aim of the rebuild less the system part. null or 0 = off (the floor alone). Preset: talky 80000, every other role null. Numeric strings are read as numbers.

compress_at.description: Without the answering model's package (`input_soft`, GH #1038), a rebuild is ordered when a call's `tokens_prompt` reaches this share of the model's own window. With one it keeps the aim of a rebuild in proportion to `input_soft`. Preset 0.5; coding and research 0.4.

rebuild_to.description: The share of the usable window a rebuild aims at. Over it, the rebuild shrinks old tool results (outside `keep_rounds`), then stubs tools unused for `stub_tools_after` rounds, then gives the summary up -- in that order. 0 = no aim. Preset 0 without a role, talky 0.45 (GH #1427), consult 0.35, coding and research 0.25.

horizon.description: How the wall is cut into segments: `day` (UTC calendar days), `task` (a `topic` mark start/end out of the memory section, and a day change, opens a segment), `all` (one segment: the rolling window of 1.0.0). Preset `all` without a role, talky `day`, the others `task`.

tiers.description: The form of a segment by its age, comma-separated, the last one for every older segment: `raw`, `summary` or `none`. Preset `raw,summary` without a role and for consult and coding, talky `raw,summary,none` (today raw, yesterday summarised, older nothing), research `raw,none`.

keep_rounds.description: How many of the newest tool iterations keep their results raw when a rebuild is over its aim -- with `gc` "1" at every rebuild (GH #1430); older results shrink to their id and one line (`history_read` brings them back), an error result never. 0 = never shrink. Preset 0 without a role, talky 1, consult 2, coding 3, research 1.

gc.description: GH #1430 (R-38-2): "1" = the garbage collection runs at every rebuild -- old tool results shrink regardless of the aim, a recall result whose row a younger raw one repeats shrinks, the scaffold of a closed delegation shrinks; "0" = the behaviour of before (tool results shrink only over the aim). Never an error result, never the person's words. Preset "1" for talky, "0" for every other role. Every rebuild writes one `gc` mark either way.

gc_scaffold.description: GH #1430 (A4): "0" switches the scaffold class of the collection off alone -- the inner `(advice)`/`(delegation)` rows of a closed delegation stay raw; the rest of the collection runs. Preset "1" for every role.

stub_tools_after.description: When a rebuild is still over its aim: a tool no call named in this many newest rounds is declared by its name and one line, `parameters` an empty object schema. 0 = never. Preset 0 without a role, talky and coding 20, consult and research 10.

window_target.description: GH #1272: the window in tokens at which the role orders a rebuild of its own (mark `target`), under the model's input_soft and without a package too; its aim is window_target x rebuild_to / compress_at, never above a soft rebuild's. 0 = off. Preset: talky 100000 (GH #1427), quick 12000, every other role 0. Numeric strings are read as numbers.

notes_share.description: GH #1303: the share of the usable window (the answering model's input_soft, at 3 characters per token) the notes block may take -- the block of `in_note` notes and `context.turn_notes` that opens the newest message of the person; over it the notes of the lowest priority are left out and said (`marks` `notes`, `hop.cuts`). 0 = no note is shown. Preset: talky 0.02, every other role 0 (quick included). Numeric strings are read as numbers.

broadcast_mode.description: Where a pin of another hive (`in_pin`) stands: `tail` -- as a message where it arrived until the next rebuild moves it into the system part (`pinned.<source>.<id>`), so a warm cache keeps its prefix -- or `system` at once. Preset `tail`.

recall_push.description: "1": the curator pushes an enriched recall ask for every turn (GH #895); empty or "0": off. Preset "1" for talky, off otherwise.

recall_budget.description: The longest recall ask the push sends, in characters (GH #895). Preset 200 for talky (the recall cell keeps no more of an ask, `memory-hive` `query_safe_chars`), 0 otherwise.

short_ids.description: "1": somebody else's words and a tool result begin with the block's short id `[#<12 hex>] ` in the window, so the model can release or pin it and read it back; the model's own answers and tool calls never do. Preset "1" for every role, off without one.

identity_budget.description: How the identity reaches the model (GH #935): `full` -- the whole identity in the system part, as before -- or `split`: the system part carries only the short form an identity pusher holds at `identity_short` (as the `identity` family), in every call; the whole identity is ONE element at the head of the window, taken at call 1, after a rebuild and after a renewal of the call's own session (and anew for another session or round), and sent byte for byte the same until the next of these, so the provider's prefix cache keeps it -- a later call takes no new snapshot, and the element is never trimmed. `split` without a short form runs as `full` and marks `identity_short_missing` once per session. Any other value keeps the preset and is said on stderr. Preset `full` for every role.

context_window.description: The model's context window in tokens when the tap does not report `hop.context_window`. 0 = unknown: without the package's `input_soft` there is then no compress trigger -- the cold cache alone orders a rebuild. No role caps the window (GH #1085).

input_soft_fallback.description: The summarizer's window in tokens before it has shown one (OR-IG-8, GH #1085): the `input_soft` of the catalogue row `input_soft_fallback_row` names, the model the curator's `./summarizer` is born on (OR-IG-9). That model is a birth token (`ctx.model`), and the llm-registry's tier for it is `light`, `openai/gpt-6-luna`. The summarizer's transcript is half of it; the stamp on its answers and a refusal over its bound replace it. Null or empty: no window known, the transcript goes whole.

input_soft_fallback_row.description: The catalogue row (`model_id` in `llm-registry/store/seed/models.jsonl`) whose `input_soft` `input_soft_fallback` is: the model the curator's `./summarizer` is born on -- a birth token (`ctx.model`) whose llm-registry tier for a small summarizer is `light` (OR-IG-9, GH #1085). A label for the reader and for the drift lock `gh1085_fallback_windows_match_the_catalog`, which holds the two together; the script does not read it. A receiver born on another model sets both.

amortise_turns.description: The turns one rebuild has to pay itself back in (GH #1038). Under the answering model's `input_soft`, a window is rebuilt when keeping its cached rest for this many turns costs more than one rebuild: `(window - aim) * cost_cached_in * N > aim * cost_in`, the prices and the soft limit out of the model's package (`hop.cost_in`, `hop.cost_cached_in`, `hop.input_soft`, stamped by the llm cell), the aim `input_soft` times `rebuild_to` / `compress_at`. Without those values the rule does not apply. Null, empty or below 1 means 10. Numeric strings are read as numbers.

max_round_plans.description: How many rounds the hive keeps a window plan for (GH #943): every round has a plan of its own, keyed by its `round_key`, and a rebuild that would leave more than this many drops the plans of the rounds whose last rebuild is oldest -- never its own -- and with each plan what its round owns: its state rows and its summary slot (GH #949). Null, empty or below 1 means 64. Numeric strings are read as numbers.

round_plan_idle_s.description: How long, in seconds, a round's window plan outlives the round's last rebuild (GH #943); a rebuild of any round drops the plans idle for longer, with what their rounds own (GH #949). A window without a rebuild lives no longer than the provider's cache, so the last rebuild is the last use. Null, empty or 0 means 2592000 (30 days). Numeric strings are read as numbers.

pending_sweep_s.description: GH #1225 (A13): a parked `pending:*` row of the ledger's `state` older than this many seconds (its `parked_at`) is taken down by the probe of the next rebuild, said as one `pending_swept` mark naming the rows that went -- on an event that comes anyway, never a timer of its own. A row without `parked_at` stays. Null, empty, zero or text = 600; below 60 counts as 60.

place.description: GH #1279, GH #1478: where the person is, as a set renders it from the profile (`Berlin`). With it (or `timezone`) every call to a target whose profile sets `frame` carries the slot `frame`: now (the call's stamp in `timezone`) and this place, facts only. Empty (the default) with `timezone` empty: no `frame` at any target. The composition sets the same value at `curator/history`.

timezone.description: GH #1279, GH #1478: the IANA zone the slot `frame` says the time in (`Europe/Berlin`); empty with a `place` = UTC, a zone this python does not know = UTC and said on stderr. Empty (the default) with `place` empty: no `frame` at any target. The composition sets the same value at `curator/history`.

live_feed.description: GH #1279, GH #1507: `1` or true = after each closed turn of a running session (the turn's seam or context carries the handle `live`, D58 live) at most ONE own feed leaves on `live_feed` with `hop.live`. What it is, the target says: the field `feed_own` of the profile its target named in `limits.profile` on its start-window ask (`./history` holds the limits as the state row `seed_limits:<live>` until the session ends); without limits or without the field it is `renew`. `renew`: when the facts a seed of the handle carries moved since the handle's last seed or feed -- the same facts `./history` puts into the seed (one rule, `seed_fact_state`): `notes` (new session and until notes, `{source, id, text}`), `inner_turns` (new advice, delegation and event turns, `{turn_id, kind}`), `topic` (the newest named topic -- a nameless `continue` mark is no topic, an `end` mark ends it), `parts` (D58 judge: the family of the start window's target `seed_target` as it stands now, `{source: {text}}`, when it moved -- never read) -- a feed without words, `hop.section` = `live_feed_section` (with `renew` also `hop.at_turn_end` "1": the target renews at the next turn boundary and then asks for the seed; the facts reach it through that seed, the feed is the signal). `context`: only what came from outside since then -- new notes and inner turns of the kind `event` (a delegation or advice turn reaches the session on its own road) -- goes as words under `payload` with `hop.section` `context`: whole units, each beginning with its place (`Notes: ` or `(<kind>) `), parted by an empty line, the newest first, greedy up to `limits.feed_budget` tokens at `limits.chars_per_token`; a unit that does not fit waits for the next closed turn, and a unit over the budget on its own goes alone and whole in a turn whose feed would be empty without it. The topic and the contributions move nothing there. `none`: no own feed. No instruction; nothing moved, nothing sent; a text turn sends nothing. The facts of the last seed (written by `./history`) or feed (written here) of a handle are the state row `seed_facts:<live>`; a handle without one compares against nothing. `0` (the default) = nothing of this is read or written.

live_feed_section.description: GH #1279: `hop.section` of a `live_feed` -- `renew` alone (the voice renews its session at the turn's end and takes the facts from the next seed; the way built). Any other value is read as `renew` and said on stderr (#1370): a `context` section carries no `payload` and no `text`, and the voice cell answers it `bad_section`.

fact_from_tool.description: GH #1407: tools or families (a list or one comma-separated string, `weather`, `web_search`) whose result is the turn's fact at once: on a running session's turn (the handle `live`, no spec call) the first tool result of a listed tool whose JSON carries a non-empty `summary` sends ONE `live_feed` with `hop.section` `fact`, `hop.fact_source` "tool" and the summary as `payload` -- the body of the splitter's sidecar -- right after the result, not after the second model round; round 2 still runs for the answer (the voice drops a later `fact` of the same `hop.turn_id`). At most one per turn (claim `pending:feed:<live>#<turn>#tool_fact`), mark `feed {section: fact, mark: {tool}}`, the road of an ordered feed (D58 feed, GH #1481). A failed or error result is never a fact. `""` (the default) = nothing read or written.

topic_aging.description: GH #1436: "1" lets the topic age -- one rule in `./history` (the topic handed to the route stamp, the judge and a seed) and `./policy` (the topic of a call's live feed): it frames no turn of a call opened after it was named, none of a session it was not last named in, and none once `topic_age_turns` turns passed without a renewed mention. "0" (the default) = the reads and answers as before, byte for byte.

topic_age_turns.description: GH #1436: with `topic_aging` "1" the turns without a renewed mention after which a topic frames no turn any more; counted by the person's rows on the wall (one per turn), not by marks.

topic_age_rows.description: GH #1436: with `topic_aging` "1" the bound of the read that counts the turns since the topic was named (the person's rows, newest first); a read that comes back full without reaching the naming counts as `topic_age_turns` turns. Keep it above `topic_age_turns`.

state_block.description: GH #1439: `1` or true = the window of a speaking way opens the person's newest message with one state line, first in the notes block: the open topic, the companion's open promises (`commitment` pins), the open errands (a delegation, a consult, a gap) and the facts set today (`fact` marks), at most `state_lines` entries; with the handover in the window, topic and promises are left to it. `0` (the default) = the window of before.

state_lines.description: GH #1439: the state line (`state_block`) names at most this many entries, the topic one of them, cut from the end. null = the preset: talky 8, every other role 0; 0 = no line. Numeric strings are read as numbers.

state_one_per_subject.description: D38 V1 (GH #1451): "1" keeps of the facts of one (subject, predicate), both set, only the youngest mark in the state line; a key with an empty half stays as before. "0": every fact of the day.

state_scheduled_on_need.description: D38 V1 (GH #1451): "1" shows a fact marked fact_kind foresight (intake fact_mark_kind "1") in the state line only in a turn whose stamp needs memory or orga, on the turn path and in the rebuild. "0": the line of before.

notes_latest_per_item.description: D38 V1 (GH #1451): "1" reads notes.item and keeps of the notes of one (source, item) only the youngest (at, then note_id) in the window; a note without an item stays. "0": the read and block of before.

summary_form.description: GH #1440 (D38 Z3, OR-38-42): the form a rebuild asks the summarizer for. `brief` = a handover brief: one line per item, `- <who> (<YYYY-MM-DD>)[ <subject>/<predicate>]: <statement>[ [<stance>]][ [superseded <YYYY-MM-DD>]][ [#<id>]]`, speakers `person`, `agent:self`, `peer:<ref>` and the kinds `topic`, `promised`, `open`, `dead_end`, `intent`; the answer is parsed line by line, an answer without one such line is rejected (old window kept, mark `summary_rejected` with `{kept, dropped}`; a mixed answer keeps its lines and says the rest in the same mark), a newer line with the same speaker and key replaces the older one in place, marked `[superseded <old date>]`, every line points at a source row of its summary, and `sources` are wall rows only. `prose` (the default, also any other value) = the chronicle of before, byte-identical.

summary_state_cond.description: GH #1440 (D38 Z3, OR-38-42): `1` or true = the transcript a rebuild hands the summarizer ends with the round's state block (promises, open points, facts set today; never the topic) as lines to keep, capped like the role's state lines; independent of `summary_form`. `0` (the default) = no list, the request of before.

summarizer_self.description: GH #1440 (D38 Z3, OR-38-42): `1` or true = a rebuild asks the role's own answer model to condense, after its answer, on the cached prefix of its last call; the answer is never spoken and never a wall row, and the summary carries the mark `summary_self`. Only compositions that wire the way back carry it. GH #1448: only while `brain` is free -- a turn of the session parked, waiting for its call, hands the summary to `./summarizer`. `0` (the default) = `./summarizer` as before.

block_prio.description: GH #1448 (D38 C2): the priority of a building block of the window plan by its kind, a JSON object kind -> whole number (higher = kept longer when stage 2 cuts for budget); a kind it does not name takes `default`, a value that is no whole number is left out. `recall_unneeded` is the recall bundle of a turn whose stamp needs no memory (`recall_by_needs`). The preset: the person's words and the answers 90, a brief 80, tool calls and results 70, state and notes 60, recall and push 40, an unneeded recall and stubs 20, the frame 100, every other kind 50.

snapshot_keep.description: GH #1448 (D38 C2, R-38-4 Nr. 5): how many plan snapshots a round keeps -- one row per call in the ledger table `snapshots` (the call's block ids with their prio and tokens), read through `./reader` (`what: "snapshots"`) behind the round's audience; the oldest beyond go when a call writes its own. Null, empty or below 1 means 32.

snapshot_window.description: GH #1462 (D58, R-38-4 Nr. 5): `1` or true = the snapshot row of every call (ledger table `snapshots`), the call of a turn and its bridge alike, also carries `sent`: canonical JSON `[{hash, kind, form, bytes}]`, one entry per element in the order it was sent -- the leaves of the system part, the identity, the messages, the tool menu. The system part is the whole tree the model holds for the call; each of its entries also says `carried`: true = this call carried the leaf, false = the model's cell held it from a call before (a first call and a bridge carry all). `hash` names the block of `blocks` that holds the bytes as sent, `bytes` their length in UTF-8; `form` is `raw` (the content whole), `stub`, `released`, `expired` or `cut` (the one-line and shortened forms), or `built` (made in the cut: the frame line, the bridge instruction, the state line, a note). The state line and the notes stand as entries of their own right before the message that carries them, and their bytes are part of that message's bytes: whoever sums sizes leaves the `built` entries out. `0` (the default): the row is written as before, without the list. The window sent never depends on it; `snapshot_keep` holds as it is.

errand_outcome.description: GH #1469 (D58): `1` or true = an errand that ends without an answer leaves its outcome in the window. The tap of a delegation round (turn `<turn>~<deadline_ms>~<hex8>`) says at the parked row `pending:delegation:<scope>#<turn>` how the round ended: `ended` "failed" with the `error_code` in the form of a code (`[a-z][a-z_]{0,31}`, never the text of a provider) when the call came back with `finish_reason` "error", `answered` 1 when a final answer reached the wall. The first curate of the session that finds such an errand failed, or past its `until` without an answer, files one wall row of kind `outcome` under the turn of the errand, at the end of the wall and in the window of that call: the first line of the `(delegation)` row and `failed` (with the code) or `no answer`; the mark `errand_outcome` `{delegation_id, outcome}` is written once per errand, and the parked row carries `outcome`. With `1` the park is written only while none stands for the turn: a second errand handed on in the same turn never parks over the first; its round gets the mark `errand_outcome` `{delegation_id, outcome: "not followed", followed}` (`followed` the id of the first errand) once, and nothing files an outcome for it. A curate of the errand's own round files nothing. The sweep of parked rows leaves a delegation row that has neither `answered` nor `outcome` while its `until` is ahead; past it, the sweep takes the row and files its outcome in the same go, in the session the park names (`errand_session`). A rebuild never shrinks the row and never counts it as scaffold; `window_lost` watches it; its prio is `block_prio.outcome`, else that of `tool_result`. A late answer arrives as before, behind the row. No timer: every check runs on a curate or a tap. `0` (the default) = no read, no write and no row more: the park is the unconditional set of before.

gc_on_cold.description: GH #1464 (D58): "1" = a rebuild for an expired cache (trigger `cache`: the lane `in_cache_expired` or the clock's refusal of the order) under its aim only collects -- the classes of the garbage collection (`gc` "1" is required), without the summarizer; the cover and the summary of the plan before stay. A collection that takes nothing leaves the window as it is and writes no plan and no mark; one that takes something writes the one `gc` mark and a `curate` mark with `curate_mark` "cold" and `cost_cents` 0. Over its aim (`cold_to`) the rebuild of before runs, with the summarizer. "0" (the default) = every rebuild for an expired cache as before. No role presets it; the set says which role gets it.

cold_to.description: GH #1464 (D58, addendum 10.11.): the aim of a rebuild for an expired cache as a share of the role's `window_target` (a number or a numeric string, `0.45` = 45 %). With `gc_on_cold` "1" the rebuild only collects under `window_target` x `cold_to` and rebuilds with the summarizer down to it above; a role without a `window_target` only collects. Empty (the default) = the aim the order of the cache inherited from the last answer, as before. No role presets it.

errand_slot.description: D58 target (N7, OR-d58-2.target.45): the family of the system tree the composite's collector writes a session's open errands into and whose `<slot>.pending` names the pending note of a running errand (since GH #1497 a note of the notes block at the tail of the window, never a leaf of the system part); a slot of one session, parked with its turn. `./intake` and `./policy` hold the same value. Empty = no such family.

lead_wired.description: D58 lead (GH #1474, OR-d58-2.lead.1): `1` = the composite wires a `lead` hive beside this curator (`templates/lead`: the edges `./curator -> ./lead` on `lead_ask`, `lead_spec`, `lead_note` and `./lead -> ./curator` setting `in_lead`); every call then asks it beside the ledger reads of `win` and waits for its verdict, a rebuild with `summary_state_cond` on and `state_lines` above 0 asks it for the session's errand, and the window tells it its notes and the events of a speculation. Anything else (shipped `0`) = no lead: nothing is asked, nothing is waited for and nothing is sent to one; every field of the verdict is empty, the call runs on the target the curate names (`hop.target`), no `lead` mark is booked, and a rebuild's bundle goes straight to the ledger with no running errand. `1` without the edges is a broken composite: the question ends as a dead letter at the hive's rim.

note_once.description: D58 note (GH #1477): `1` = a note of scope `once` (`./intake` `in_note`, with its own knob on) stands in the calls of exactly one turn, like a `turn` note: the turn's first call shows it, every later call of the turn shows the same block, no later turn sees it. It is used up only when a window showed it -- left out for want of room it stays open and is said as dropped in the mark `notes` -- as a conditional write of `used_turn` (only while empty, so of two writers exactly one holds). A shown note that carries `receipt` answers on the route `note_receipt` in the same step as the call's sends, every field in the head (`note_source`, `note_id`, `receipt`, `session_id`, `turn_id`, `target`, `at`). A spec call books nothing when it leaves: what its window showed waits in the lead (`spec_go`) and is booked when its answer is kept; a call held behind a speculation books when its sends are released; a call thrown away books nothing. A `once` note never rides a live feed. `turn` notes stay as they are. `0` (shipped) = `once` is no scope, the column `receipt` is never read: the window of before, byte for byte. Switch it with the same knob on `./intake` and `./history`.

feed_in.description: D58 feed (GH #1481): `1` or true = the lane `in_feed` takes orders from outside: an order to feed a running session now goes out at once as ONE `live_feed` -- the head as ordered (`live`, `session_id`, `turn_id`, `section`, `sender`, `at_turn_end` and every other field passed on; the round from `hop.audience_set`, else the context), the body as ordered without its field `mark` -- with ONE mark `feed {section, sender, once?, mark?}` in the same step; with `hop.once` only where the claim `pending:feed:<live>#<turn>#<once>` took (one round trip); no `live`: booked with `reason` `no_live`, never sent; the id of a `once` note (`body.source`, `body.id`): booked `once_note`; a note a seed of the handle carries is entered into `seed_facts:<live>` (compare-and-set). `0` (the default) = the lane takes nothing: nothing read, written or sent.

seed_target.description: D58 judge (GH #1480): the target whose family a start window (`seed`) and the live facts and live feed of a running session carry -- the contributions the domains leave for it (`in_part`, a curate's `parts`), one fact per source, never read. The same name in `./history` and `./policy`. "" (the default) = none.

part_rows.description: D58 judge (GH #1480): the most contributions one read of a target's family takes, per range (the contributions without a subject, and those about the round's person); a read that comes back full is said on stderr. The same number in `./history` and `./policy`.

class_notes.description: GH #1279, GH #1478: what the curator does for a turn by the class of its route stamp (`hop.path`, else `context.path`), as `{class: {text, tools, pair}}`; which class a turn has is the composition's model's word, never the curator's. Not applied on the turn that answers an errand (`consult_id`). `text`: ONE turn note of such a turn (id the class, source `curator`, scope `turn`, priority 0, shown under `notes_share` like every note); empty = no note. `tools` "none": no tool at any target (`tool_scope` `{allow: []}`, the channel's deny kept) and no frozen system part of the turn (no `turn_system:` row: a turn without a tool has no tool rounds). `pair`: the field the pair travels under -- the assistant's final answer to such a turn (sidecar block left out), the person's words of the session's next turn and the class that turn's stamp resolved to go to the affinity as ONE `propose` (route `propose`, a `tool_call` turn `<class>-<asked turn>` with `{op: propose, id: <class>:<uuid5 of session#turn>, source_ref: curator:<class>:<session>#<turn>, entity_ref, field_path: <pair>, value: {question, answer, class, session_id, asked_turn, answered_turn}}`, `entity_ref` the round's one entry that is no `agent:`), exactly once: the row `<class>:<session>` (`{turn, call, at}`) is taken by key and value first. Without `pair` nothing is kept. `{}` (the default): the curator names no class and does nothing of this. Replaces `clarify_note` (removed): a set that used it sets `{"clarify": {"text": <its note>, "tools": "none", "pair": "mx.hints.clarify"}}`. D54g GH #1506: a key may also be `<class>/<move>` -- the entry of a turn whose stamp carries that move beside the class (`hop.move`; the move is a name of the composition's own list, the curator knows none). Its `text` is then the turn's note IN PLACE of the class's; without such an entry the class's entry stands, without either there is no note. Of an entry with a move only `text` counts: `tools` and `pair` are not read (a line on stderr says so), and those of the class's own entry stay in force -- a move changes what is said, never the target, the way or the tools of the turn, and it is not part of the question to the lead.

carry_notes.description: GH #1436: the after-effect of a turn note, as `{source: {text, until, priority?}}`. A turn whose turn notes hold a note of a named source leaves a note `carry.<source>` (scope `until`, one per source and round) with this `text`; it shows only in LATER sessions -- never in the session it was born in -- and a turn with a fresh note of the same source shows that one instead. `until`: seconds after the turn, or "day" (the end of the turn's day in `timezone`, UTC without one). Shipped {}: no row, every window as before.

notes.description: GH #1279: on `live_feed` -- the session and until notes new since the call's last seed or feed, `{source, id, text}`.

inner_turns.description: GH #1279: on `live_feed` -- the inner turns (advice, delegation, event) new since the call's last seed or feed, `{turn_id, kind}`.

topic.description: GH #1279: on `live_feed` -- the newest named topic, when it moved since the call's last seed or feed ("" once a topic ended).

section.description: On `live_feed`: the section of the feed the body carries -- a field of an ordered body, passed on unchanged (a conditional feed of the verdict, D58 moveout, GH #1476; an order on `in_feed`, D58 feed); GH #1407: `fact` on a tool fact (`fact_from_tool`).

seconds.description: D58 moveout (GH #1476): on `live_feed` -- a field of an ordered body, passed on unchanged (a conditional feed of the verdict, an order on `in_feed`); the curator reads none of it (before the move GH #1400 built it here).

way.description: D58 moveout (GH #1476): on `live_feed` -- a field of an ordered body, passed on unchanged (a conditional feed of the verdict, an order on `in_feed`); the curator reads none of it (before the move GH #1400 built it here).

family.description: D58 moveout (GH #1476): on `live_feed` -- a field of an ordered body, passed on unchanged (a conditional feed of the verdict, an order on `in_feed`); the curator reads none of it (before the move GH #1400 built it here).

params.description: GH #1450: on `catalog_ask` -- the empty params slot the model cell answers with its row.

parts.description: D58 judge (GH #1480): on `live_feed` -- the family of the start window's target (`seed_target`), one leaf `{text}` per source as the domains left it, when it moved since the call's last seed or feed.

interim.description: GH #1260: "tool" on the required call of a simple turn's tool round -- an answer of it without a call is not said, and the curator gives the round to the brain (`escalate`, reason `no_tool_call`). The composite's edge lifts it into `context.interim` for the dispatcher. A side call of that round says `round_open` instead (D58 moveout).

spec.description: GH #1275: "1" on a spec call of the quick voice (`quick_speculative`); the composite's edge lifts it into `context.spec`, and the answer comes back on `in_spec_llm`, never to the splitter.

section.description: GH #1279: on `live_feed` -- the param `live_feed_section` (`renew`) for an own feed to a target whose `feed_own` is `renew` or unnamed; `context` for one whose `feed_own` is `context` (GH #1507: words under `payload`, whole units each beginning with its place, parted by an empty line, at most `limits.feed_budget` tokens except one unit over the budget on its own, which goes alone); or the section a conditional feed of the verdict names (D58 moveout, GH #1476), or `fact` (GH #1407, `fact_from_tool`); the composite's edge sets the `call_id` of the running session's model cell from `hop.live`. D58 feed (GH #1481): on an order on `in_feed` the orderer's name, passed on (the receiver takes what it knows).

fact_source.description: GH #1407: on `live_feed` `fact` -- "tool": the fact is a listed tool's summary (`fact_from_tool`), the summary a string in body `payload` (left undeclared: the gap section passes on to `./push` with an object `payload`); the voice drops a later `fact` of the same `hop.turn_id`.

at_turn_end.description: GH #1279: on `live_feed` with `section` `renew` -- "1": the voice cell takes it at the next turn boundary only. Never on a conditional feed of the verdict (GH #1400; D58 moveout, GH #1476). D58 feed (GH #1481): on an order on `in_feed` passed on as ordered, never set by the curator.

live.description: GH #1279, D58 live: on `live_feed` -- the handle of the running session the turn belongs to (its seam's or context's `live`).

catalog_for.description: GH #1450: on `catalog_ask` -- the model cell asked for its catalogue row (`brain`, `quick`, `quick_spec`).

note_source.description: D58 note (GH #1477): on `note_receipt` -- the `source` of the shown note.

note_id.description: D58 note (GH #1477): on `note_receipt` -- the `id` of the shown note.

receipt.description: D58 note (GH #1477): on `note_receipt` -- the note's `receipt` as its sender gave it, never read by the curator.

at.description: D58 note (GH #1477): on `note_receipt` -- the time of the call that showed the note.

sender.description: D58 feed (GH #1481): on `live_feed` of an order on `in_feed` -- the orderer, as the order or its edge set it; passed on, booked in the mark `feed`.

once.description: D58 feed (GH #1481): on `live_feed` of an order on `in_feed` -- the orderer's key of "at most once per turn" (claim `pending:feed:<live>#<turn>#<once>`), passed on.

session_id.description: D58 note (GH #1477): on `note_receipt` -- the session the note was shown in.

turn_id.description: D58 note (GH #1477): on `note_receipt` -- the turn whose window showed the note.

target.description: D58 note (GH #1477): on `note_receipt` -- the target of the call that showed the note ("" when the call named none).

call_kind.description: D58 moveout (GH #1476): the kind of a model call -- "side" on a side call (the lead's `side`), "fallback" on the call that takes on a round its first call handed on; none on a main call. The composite's edges lift it into `context.call_kind`, so it comes back with the answer; the ending of the call id is not read.

round_open.description: D58 moveout (GH #1476): "1" on a side call whose answer does not end the round (condition `must_call`: the tool result is still to come). A composite's edge may lift it into the context of the call.

description.purpose: The window and the record of one model, by the policy of its role. On every call it builds the window deterministically from the ledger and the current plan (the slots, pins and tool stubs as the system part, sent only when a family changed; the wall after the plan's cover as the messages, each block in the form the plan gave it and, with short ids on, with its id in front), writes the call record and its block list, and sends the call. The tap fills the record and sets the clock; a cold cache or a crossed `compress_at` of the usable window starts a rebuild: the plan made anew from the role's segments and tiers, the model's releases and pins applied, a summary through `./summarizer` when a segment is to be condensed -- at most one at a time.
description.not_in_scope: No wall writes, no marks and no episodes. No model call on the hot path: the rebuild runs on a message of its own and the call that triggered it is already gone. Nothing a model releases disappears: the ledger keeps every block byte for byte, the window shows it as one line.
description.emits_meaning: lstore: ledger operations. brain: the call, leaving the hive. clock: one timer order per round, `add` with `rearm` under the round's own id (GH #904, GH #943); never a `remove`. summarize: the condensation request for `./summarizer`. push_ask, push_gap: the push's two doors (`in_recall_ask`, the section `gap`), handed on to `./push` with `recall_push`, `recall_budget` and `short_ids` on the hop, as the role resolved them. handover: the first call of a session this window did not serve last, handed to `./handover` once (`session_id`, `turn_id`, `curator_call`); it comes back as the store answer `handover-done`, and the window is read from here as for any call (GH #896).
description.consumes_meaning: The ledger's answers to its phases (win-hashes, win, relay, tap, rb-probe, rb-claim, rb-data, rb-send, sum, done, reg, dropped, handover-done, win-plan), the clock's strike (`in_cache_expired`, `in_clock_error`) and the summarizer's answer (`in_summary`), and the push's two doors on their way to `./push` (`in_recall_ask`, `in_section` with the section `gap`).
